vi.finger_lesson_13_has_3_parts_13a_major_1: Bài 13 gồm 3 phần: 13A Trưởng → 13B Em7/E7 → 13C Thứ
vi.finger_roots_on_strings_5_and_2_the_c_ma: Gốc trên dây 5 và dây 2; vùng C trưởng mẫu nằm ở ngăn 0-3
vi.finger_roots_on_strings_5_and_3_the_c_ma: Gốc trên dây 5 và dây 3; vùng C trưởng mẫu nằm ở ngăn 2-6
vi.finger_roots_on_strings_6_3_and_1_the_c_: Gốc trên dây 6, dây 3 và dây 1; vùng C trưởng mẫu nằm ở ngăn 5-8
vi.finger_roots_on_strings_6_4_and_1_the_c_: Gốc trên dây 6, dây 4 và dây 1; vùng C trưởng mẫu nằm ở ngăn 7-10
vi.finger_roots_on_strings_4_and_2_the_c_ma: Gốc trên dây 4 và dây 2; vùng C trưởng mẫu nằm ở ngăn 9-13
vi.finger_ionian_is_the_standard_major_scal: Ionian là âm giai trưởng chuẩn. Bậc 7 trưởng tạo lực hút rõ về nốt gốc.
vi.finger_use_it_over_major_and_maj7_harmon: Dùng trên hợp âm trưởng, maj7 và các giai điệu trưởng thông dụng.
vi.finger_dorian_is_a_minor_mode_with_a_nat: Dorian là mode thứ có bậc 6 trưởng. Bậc 6 giúp màu thứ sáng và linh hoạt hơn Aeolian.
vi.finger_useful_over_m7_and_m6_harmony_fun: Phù hợp hợp âm m7, m6, funk, jazz và các vòng hòa âm Dorian.
vi.finger_phrygian_is_a_minor_mode_whose_ch: Phrygian là mode thứ có bậc ♭2 đặc trưng, tạo cảm giác tối và căng gần nốt gốc.
vi.finger_useful_over_static_minor_harmony_: Phù hợp các nền hợp âm thứ tĩnh, metal và màu âm Tây Ban Nha; không đồng nhất với Phrygian dominant.
vi.finger_lydian_is_a_major_mode_with_a_cha: Lydian là mode trưởng có bậc ♯4 đặc trưng, tạo màu sáng, rộng và ít va chạm với bậc 3.
vi.finger_useful_over_maj7_and_maj711_harmo: Phù hợp hợp âm maj7, maj7♯11 và các nền trưởng cần màu sắc bay, hiện đại.
vi.finger_mixolydian_is_a_major_mode_with_a: Mixolydian là mode trưởng có bậc ♭7. Cặp 3 trưởng và ♭7 thể hiện rõ chức năng dominant.
vi.finger_use_it_over_dominant_seventh_harm: Dùng trên hợp âm dominant 7, blues, rock, funk và các vòng hòa âm Mixolydian.
vi.finger_aeolian_is_the_natural_minor_scal: Aeolian chính là âm giai thứ tự nhiên. Bậc ♭6 là màu quan trọng phân biệt với Dorian.
vi.finger_use_it_over_minor_harmony_natural: Dùng trên hợp âm thứ, các vòng hòa âm thứ tự nhiên và giai điệu có màu buồn, ổn định.
vi.finger_locrian_is_a_minor_mode_with_a_5_: Locrian là mode thứ có ♭5 và ♭2, nên hợp âm chủ không ổn định như các mode còn lại.
vi.finger_useful_over_m75_half_diminished_h: Phù hợp hợp âm m7♭5 (half-diminished), bài tập nghe và các đoạn cần độ căng cao.

en.finger_ionian_is_the_standard_major_scal: Ionian is the standard major scale. Its major 7th creates a strong pull toward the tonic.

en.finger_dorian_is_a_minor_mode_with_a_nat: Dorian is a minor mode with a natural 6th, giving it a brighter sound than Aeolian.
en.finger_useful_over_m7_and_m6_harmony_fun: Useful over m7 and m6 harmony, funk, jazz and Dorian vamps.
en.finger_phrygian_is_a_minor_mode_whose_ch: Phrygian is a minor mode whose characteristic ♭2 creates a dark, tense pull near the tonic.
en.finger_useful_over_static_minor_harmony_: Useful over static minor harmony, metal and Spanish-flavoured lines; it is not the same as Phrygian dominant.
en.finger_lydian_is_a_major_mode_with_a_cha: Lydian is a major mode with a characteristic ♯4, producing a bright and open sound.
en.finger_useful_over_maj7_and_maj711_harmo: Useful over maj7 and maj7♯11 harmony and modern, floating major sounds.
en.finger_mixolydian_is_a_major_mode_with_a: Mixolydian is a major mode with a ♭7. The major 3rd and ♭7 clearly outline dominant function.
en.finger_use_it_over_dominant_seventh_harm: Use it over dominant-seventh harmony, blues, rock, funk and Mixolydian progressions.
en.finger_aeolian_is_the_natural_minor_scal: Aeolian is the natural minor scale. Its ♭6 is an important contrast with Dorian.
en.finger_use_it_over_minor_harmony_natural: Use it over minor harmony, natural-minor progressions and stable, darker melodies.
en.finger_locrian_is_a_minor_mode_with_a_5_: Locrian is a minor mode with a ♭5 and ♭2, so its tonic harmony is inherently unstable.
en.finger_useful_over_m75_half_diminished_h: Useful over m7♭5 (half-diminished) harmony, ear training and highly tense passages.
en.finger_harmonic_minor_raises_the_7th_of_: Harmonic minor raises the 7th of natural minor. The ♭6–7 span creates a strong pull to the tonic and its characteristic harmonic colour.
en.finger_use_it_in_minor_key_harmony_espec: Use it in minor-key harmony, especially V7 resolving to i, as well as classical metal, neoclassical and many flamenco contexts.
en.finger_this_is_the_jazz_melodic_minor_fo: This is the jazz melodic-minor form: the same collection ascending and descending. It can be heard as a major scale with a lowered 3rd.
en.finger_use_it_over_m_maj7_and_m6_harmony: Use it over m(maj7) and m6 harmony and as the parent scale of Lydian dominant, Altered and the other melodic-minor modes.
en.finger_a_bright_accessible_pentatonic_sc: A bright, accessible pentatonic scale with few avoid notes.
en.finger_useful_for_pop_country_and_soloin: Useful for pop, country and soloing over major chords.
en.finger_the_familiar_minor_pentatonic_sou: The familiar minor pentatonic sound used in blues and rock.
en.finger_useful_for_blues_rock_and_soloing: Useful for blues, rock and soloing over minor chords.
en.finger_a_variant_formed_by_omitting_degr: A variant formed by omitting degrees 2 and 6 from Mixolydian. “With 4” is shown because methods do not use one universal naming convention.
en.finger_keeps_the_major_3rd_and_7_and_add: Keeps the major 3rd and ♭7 and adds the 4th; useful over dominant 7, 7sus4, funk and rock.
en.finger_a_dominant_seventh_outline_plus_d: A dominant-seventh outline plus degree 2/9. Some methods also call it Mixolydian pentatonic.
en.finger_useful_over_dominant_7_9_harmony_: Useful over dominant 7/9 harmony in jazz, blues and funk, especially when avoiding the 4th.
en.finger_the_major_blues_scale_is_major_pe: The major blues scale is major pentatonic plus ♭3. The expressive tension between ♭3 and 3 creates its blues colour.
en.finger_useful_for_major_blues_country_an: Useful for major blues, country and rock and roll over major or dominant harmony, treating ♭3 as a blue note.
en.finger_the_minor_blues_scale_is_minor_pe: The minor blues scale is minor pentatonic plus ♭5. The ♭5 is its characteristic blue note, often approached or bent toward 5.
en.finger_useful_for_blues_and_rock_over_mi: Useful for blues and rock over minor or dominant harmony, depending on the harmonic context.
en.finger_the_second_mode_of_melodic_minor_: The second mode of melodic minor. It keeps Dorian's natural 6th while adding a dark, tense ♭2.
en.finger_useful_over_m7_9_minor_sus_harmon: Useful over m7(♭9), minor-sus harmony and jazz/fusion passages requiring a darker Dorian colour.
en.finger_the_third_mode_of_melodic_minor_c: The third mode of melodic minor, combining Lydian's ♯4 with the augmented chord's ♯5.
en.finger_use_it_over_maj75_maj7115_and_mod: Use it over maj7♯5, maj7♯11♯5 and modern augmented-major harmony.
en.finger_the_fourth_mode_of_melodic_minor_: The fourth mode of melodic minor, also called Lydian ♭7. It combines ♯4/♯11 with the dominant major 3rd and ♭7.
en.finger_use_it_over_711_chords_non_resolv: Use it over 7♯11 chords, non-resolving dominants, jazz and fusion.
en.finger_the_fifth_mode_of_melodic_minor_i: The fifth mode of melodic minor. It is Mixolydian with a ♭6, producing a darker dominant sound with a minor inflection.
en.finger_use_it_over_7_13_dominants_resolv: Use it over 7(♭13), dominants resolving to minor and cinematic dominant harmony.
en.finger_the_sixth_mode_of_melodic_minor_c: The sixth mode of melodic minor. Compared with ordinary Locrian, its natural 2nd softens the tension next to the tonic.
en.finger_use_it_over_m75_when_a_natural_9_: Use it over m7♭5 when a natural 9 fits the harmony, especially in minor jazz ii–V–i progressions.
en.finger_the_seventh_mode_of_melodic_minor: The seventh mode of melodic minor. Beyond 1, 3 and ♭7, it contains the altered dominant tensions ♭9, ♯9, ♭5/♯11 and ♭13.
en.finger_use_it_over_7alt_79_79_75_or_713_: Use it over 7alt, 7♭9, 7♯9, 7♭5 or 7♭13 when a dominant chord requires strong resolution.
en.finger_the_second_mode_of_harmonic_minor: The second mode of harmonic minor. It keeps Locrian's ♭2 and ♭5 while raising ♭6 to a natural 6th.
en.finger_use_it_over_m75_when_a_natural_13: Use it over m7♭5 when a natural 13 fits, or for a brighter half-diminished colour than ordinary Locrian.
en.finger_the_third_mode_of_harmonic_minor_: The third mode of harmonic minor. It is Ionian with a ♯5, creating a maj7♯5 tonic while retaining a natural 4th.
en.finger_use_it_over_maj75_and_augmented_m: Use it over maj7♯5 and augmented-major harmony when the natural 4th is preferred to Lydian augmented's ♯4.
en.finger_the_fourth_mode_of_harmonic_minor: The fourth mode of harmonic minor. It keeps Dorian's natural 6th while replacing the natural 4th with ♯4.
en.finger_use_it_over_m711_fusion_metal_and: Use it over m7♯11, fusion, metal and minor vamps requiring a brighter yet tenser colour than ordinary Dorian.
en.finger_the_fifth_mode_of_harmonic_minor_: The fifth mode of harmonic minor. Its ♭2 combined with a major 3rd creates a distinctive dominant sound unlike ordinary Phrygian.
en.finger_use_it_over_v7_in_minor_keys_9_13: Use it over V7 in minor keys, ♭9/♭13 dominants, metal, fusion and many flamenco contexts.
en.finger_the_sixth_mode_of_harmonic_minor_: The sixth mode of harmonic minor. It combines ♯2 with Lydian's ♯4, creating an augmented second near the tonic.
en.finger_use_it_over_maj711_when_a_9_2_fit: Use it over maj7♯11 when a ♯9/♯2 fits the line, mainly in advanced composition and jazz contexts.
en.finger_the_seventh_mode_of_harmonic_mino: The seventh mode of harmonic minor. It is highly tense, with ♭4, ♭5 and a doubly lowered 7th; it is not the melodic-minor Altered/Super Locrian scale.
en.finger_use_sparingly_in_composition_dimi: Use sparingly in composition, diminished/altered harmony and advanced ear training; always read it together with its formula.
en.finger_a_six_note_scale_built_entirely_f: A six-note scale built entirely from whole steps. With no semitones, it sounds floating and unresolved.
en.finger_use_it_over_augmented_harmony_and: Use it over augmented harmony and dominant chords with ♯5/♭5 for an ambiguous, symmetrical colour.
en.finger_an_eight_note_symmetrical_scale_a: An eight-note symmetrical scale alternating half and whole steps. It contains a dominant chord plus several altered tensions.
en.finger_use_it_over_79_79_139_and_dominan: Use it over 7♭9, 7♯9, 13♭9 and dominant-diminished harmony, especially before resolution.
en.finger_an_eight_note_symmetrical_scale_a: An eight-note symmetrical scale alternating whole and half steps. It outlines a diminished-seventh chord from the tonic.
en.finger_use_it_over_7_harmony_diminished_: Use it over °7 harmony, diminished sequences and minor-third transposition practice.
en.finger_the_chromatic_scale_contains_all_: The chromatic scale contains all 12 pitch classes in the octave. It is not a major-scale mode but the complete semitone collection.
en.finger_use_it_for_technique_chromatic_ap: Use it for technique, chromatic approaches between chord tones, semitone ear training and chromatic line development.
en.finger_mixolydian_plus_a_major_7th_passi: Mixolydian plus a major 7th passing tone. With suitable rhythmic placement, chord tones can align consistently with strong beats.
en.finger_use_it_over_dominant_seventh_harm: Use it over dominant-seventh harmony in bebop and jazz; practise it rhythmically rather than only as a mechanical up-and-down scale.
en.finger_a_major_scale_with_a_lowered_6th_: A major scale with a lowered 6th, combining a major tonic with the ♭6 colour often associated with minor harmony.
en.finger_use_it_over_maj7_13_borrowed_harm: Use it over maj7(♭13), borrowed harmony and major-key lines requiring a darker colour.
en.finger_a_major_scale_with_2_and_6_creati: A major scale with ♭2 and ♭6, creating two characteristic augmented seconds. Some Western sources also call it Byzantine.
en.finger_use_it_for_western_labelled_middl: Use it for Western-labelled Middle Eastern/Mediterranean colours, metal, fusion and composition requiring strong tension.
en.finger_ritusen_yo_pentatonic_mode_12456_: Ritusen/Yo pentatonic mode: 1–2–4–5–6. With G as tonic, G–A–C–D–E shares the pitches of C major pentatonic, so its open C-reference shape is valid while G stays the root (R). This differs from dominant 1–3–4–5–b7.
en.finger_use_for_open_suspended_pentatonic: Use for open/suspended pentatonic sounds. In G, the C-major reference shape occupies open strings through fret 4; keep G as the tonal centre.
en.finger_tuner_tools_uses_the_common_weste: Tuner Tools uses the common Western reference form 1–2–♭3–5–♭6. Naming and pitches can vary with tuning, instrument and Japanese tradition.
en.finger_useful_for_pentatonic_melody_writ: Useful for pentatonic melody writing with wide gaps, a dark colour and interval-control practice.
en.finger_the_western_reference_form_12457_: The Western reference form 1–♭2–4–5–♭7 creates a dark suspended colour. Traditional terminology can vary by source and tuning.
en.finger_useful_over_sus_harmony_dark_melo: Useful over sus harmony, dark melody, ambient, metal and exercises emphasizing the ♭2.
en.finger_the_western_reference_form_12457_: The Western reference form 1–♭2–4–♭5–♭7 has strongly tense ♭2 and ♭5 degrees. Its historical name should not be treated as one absolutely fixed Western mode.
en.finger_useful_for_dark_melody_sound_desi: Useful for dark melody, sound design, metal and ear training with tense intervals.
en.finger_a_custom_roman_numeral_loop_that_: A custom Roman-numeral loop that is saved automatically and transposes to every key.
en.finger_the_dominant_of_the_target_chord_: The dominant of the target chord; its 3rd and 7th pull clearly into {0}.
en.finger_the_diminished_chord_root_lies_a_: The diminished chord root lies a semitone below {0}, resolving upward into the destination root.
en.finger_a_dominant_a_semitone_above_the_t: A dominant a semitone above the target, useful in jazz with a strong chromatic bass line.
en.finger_keep_the_hand_relaxed_and_play_1_: Keep the hand relaxed and play 1-2-3-4 evenly across six strings.

es.finger_roots_on_strings_5_and_2_the_c_ma: Roots on strings 5 and 2; the C-major reference box spans frets 0-3
es.finger_roots_on_strings_5_and_3_the_c_ma: Roots on strings 5 and 3; the C-major reference box spans frets 2-6
es.finger_roots_on_strings_6_3_and_1_the_c_: Roots on strings 6, 3 and 1; the C-major reference box spans frets 5-8
es.finger_roots_on_strings_6_4_and_1_the_c_: Roots on strings 6, 4 and 1; the C-major reference box spans frets 7-10

es.finger_ionian_is_the_standard_major_scal: Ionian is the standard major scale. Its major 7th creates a strong pull toward the tonic.
es.finger_use_it_over_major_and_maj7_harmon: Use it over major and maj7 harmony and conventional major-key melodies.
es.finger_dorian_is_a_minor_mode_with_a_nat: Dorian is a minor mode with a natural 6th, giving it a brighter sound than Aeolian.
es.finger_useful_over_m7_and_m6_harmony_fun: Useful over m7 and m6 harmony, funk, jazz and Dorian vamps.
es.finger_phrygian_is_a_minor_mode_whose_ch: Phrygian is a minor mode whose characteristic ♭2 creates a dark, tense pull near the tonic.
es.finger_useful_over_static_minor_harmony_: Useful over static minor harmony, metal and Spanish-flavoured lines; it is not the same as Phrygian dominant.
es.finger_lydian_is_a_major_mode_with_a_cha: Lydian is a major mode with a characteristic ♯4, producing a bright and open sound.
es.finger_useful_over_maj7_and_maj711_harmo: Useful over maj7 and maj7♯11 harmony and modern, floating major sounds.
es.finger_mixolydian_is_a_major_mode_with_a: Mixolydian is a major mode with a ♭7. The major 3rd and ♭7 clearly outline dominant function.
es.finger_use_it_over_dominant_seventh_harm: Use it over dominant-seventh harmony, blues, rock, funk and Mixolydian progressions.
es.finger_aeolian_is_the_natural_minor_scal: Aeolian is the natural minor scale. Its ♭6 is an important contrast with Dorian.
es.finger_use_it_over_minor_harmony_natural: Use it over minor harmony, natural-minor progressions and stable, darker melodies.
es.finger_locrian_is_a_minor_mode_with_a_5_: Locrian is a minor mode with a ♭5 and ♭2, so its tonic harmony is inherently unstable.
es.finger_useful_over_m75_half_diminished_h: Useful over m7♭5 (half-diminished) harmony, ear training and highly tense passages.
es.finger_harmonic_minor_raises_the_7th_of_: Harmonic minor raises the 7th of natural minor. The ♭6–7 span creates a strong pull to the tonic and its characteristic harmonic colour.
es.finger_use_it_in_minor_key_harmony_espec: Use it in minor-key harmony, especially V7 resolving to i, as well as classical metal, neoclassical and many flamenco contexts.
es.finger_this_is_the_jazz_melodic_minor_fo: This is the jazz melodic-minor form: the same collection ascending and descending. It can be heard as a major scale with a lowered 3rd.
es.finger_use_it_over_m_maj7_and_m6_harmony: Use it over m(maj7) and m6 harmony and as the parent scale of Lydian dominant, Altered and the other melodic-minor modes.
es.finger_a_bright_accessible_pentatonic_sc: A bright, accessible pentatonic scale with few avoid notes.
es.finger_useful_for_pop_country_and_soloin: Useful for pop, country and soloing over major chords.
es.finger_the_familiar_minor_pentatonic_sou: The familiar minor pentatonic sound used in blues and rock.
es.finger_useful_for_blues_rock_and_soloing: Useful for blues, rock and soloing over minor chords.
es.finger_a_variant_formed_by_omitting_degr: A variant formed by omitting degrees 2 and 6 from Mixolydian. “With 4” is shown because methods do not use one universal naming convention.
es.finger_keeps_the_major_3rd_and_7_and_add: Keeps the major 3rd and ♭7 and adds the 4th; useful over dominant 7, 7sus4, funk and rock.
es.finger_a_dominant_seventh_outline_plus_d: A dominant-seventh outline plus degree 2/9. Some methods also call it Mixolydian pentatonic.
es.finger_useful_over_dominant_7_9_harmony_: Useful over dominant 7/9 harmony in jazz, blues and funk, especially when avoiding the 4th.
es.finger_the_major_blues_scale_is_major_pe: The major blues scale is major pentatonic plus ♭3. The expressive tension between ♭3 and 3 creates its blues colour.
es.finger_useful_for_major_blues_country_an: Useful for major blues, country and rock and roll over major or dominant harmony, treating ♭3 as a blue note.
es.finger_the_minor_blues_scale_is_minor_pe: The minor blues scale is minor pentatonic plus ♭5. The ♭5 is its characteristic blue note, often approached or bent toward 5.
es.finger_useful_for_blues_and_rock_over_mi: Useful for blues and rock over minor or dominant harmony, depending on the harmonic context.
es.finger_the_second_mode_of_melodic_minor_: The second mode of melodic minor. It keeps Dorian's natural 6th while adding a dark, tense ♭2.
es.finger_useful_over_m7_9_minor_sus_harmon: Useful over m7(♭9), minor-sus harmony and jazz/fusion passages requiring a darker Dorian colour.
es.finger_the_third_mode_of_melodic_minor_c: The third mode of melodic minor, combining Lydian's ♯4 with the augmented chord's ♯5.
es.finger_use_it_over_maj75_maj7115_and_mod: Use it over maj7♯5, maj7♯11♯5 and modern augmented-major harmony.
es.finger_the_fourth_mode_of_melodic_minor_: The fourth mode of melodic minor, also called Lydian ♭7. It combines ♯4/♯11 with the dominant major 3rd and ♭7.
es.finger_use_it_over_711_chords_non_resolv: Use it over 7♯11 chords, non-resolving dominants, jazz and fusion.
es.finger_the_fifth_mode_of_melodic_minor_i: The fifth mode of melodic minor. It is Mixolydian with a ♭6, producing a darker dominant sound with a minor inflection.
es.finger_use_it_over_7_13_dominants_resolv: Use it over 7(♭13), dominants resolving to minor and cinematic dominant harmony.
es.finger_the_sixth_mode_of_melodic_minor_c: The sixth mode of melodic minor. Compared with ordinary Locrian, its natural 2nd softens the tension next to the tonic.
es.finger_use_it_over_m75_when_a_natural_9_: Use it over m7♭5 when a natural 9 fits the harmony, especially in minor jazz ii–V–i progressions.
es.finger_the_seventh_mode_of_melodic_minor: The seventh mode of melodic minor. Beyond 1, 3 and ♭7, it contains the altered dominant tensions ♭9, ♯9, ♭5/♯11 and ♭13.
es.finger_use_it_over_7alt_79_79_75_or_713_: Use it over 7alt, 7♭9, 7♯9, 7♭5 or 7♭13 when a dominant chord requires strong resolution.
es.finger_the_second_mode_of_harmonic_minor: The second mode of harmonic minor. It keeps Locrian's ♭2 and ♭5 while raising ♭6 to a natural 6th.
es.finger_use_it_over_m75_when_a_natural_13: Use it over m7♭5 when a natural 13 fits, or for a brighter half-diminished colour than ordinary Locrian.
es.finger_the_third_mode_of_harmonic_minor_: The third mode of harmonic minor. It is Ionian with a ♯5, creating a maj7♯5 tonic while retaining a natural 4th.
es.finger_use_it_over_maj75_and_augmented_m: Use it over maj7♯5 and augmented-major harmony when the natural 4th is preferred to Lydian augmented's ♯4.
es.finger_the_fourth_mode_of_harmonic_minor: The fourth mode of harmonic minor. It keeps Dorian's natural 6th while replacing the natural 4th with ♯4.
es.finger_use_it_over_m711_fusion_metal_and: Use it over m7♯11, fusion, metal and minor vamps requiring a brighter yet tenser colour than ordinary Dorian.
es.finger_the_fifth_mode_of_harmonic_minor_: The fifth mode of harmonic minor. Its ♭2 combined with a major 3rd creates a distinctive dominant sound unlike ordinary Phrygian.
es.finger_use_it_over_v7_in_minor_keys_9_13: Use it over V7 in minor keys, ♭9/♭13 dominants, metal, fusion and many flamenco contexts.
es.finger_the_sixth_mode_of_harmonic_minor_: The sixth mode of harmonic minor. It combines ♯2 with Lydian's ♯4, creating an augmented second near the tonic.
es.finger_use_it_over_maj711_when_a_9_2_fit: Use it over maj7♯11 when a ♯9/♯2 fits the line, mainly in advanced composition and jazz contexts.
es.finger_the_seventh_mode_of_harmonic_mino: The seventh mode of harmonic minor. It is highly tense, with ♭4, ♭5 and a doubly lowered 7th; it is not the melodic-minor Altered/Super Locrian scale.
es.finger_use_sparingly_in_composition_dimi: Use sparingly in composition, diminished/altered harmony and advanced ear training; always read it together with its formula.
es.finger_a_six_note_scale_built_entirely_f: A six-note scale built entirely from whole steps. With no semitones, it sounds floating and unresolved.
es.finger_use_it_over_augmented_harmony_and: Use it over augmented harmony and dominant chords with ♯5/♭5 for an ambiguous, symmetrical colour.
es.finger_an_eight_note_symmetrical_scale_a: An eight-note symmetrical scale alternating half and whole steps. It contains a dominant chord plus several altered tensions.
es.finger_use_it_over_79_79_139_and_dominan: Use it over 7♭9, 7♯9, 13♭9 and dominant-diminished harmony, especially before resolution.
es.finger_an_eight_note_symmetrical_scale_a: An eight-note symmetrical scale alternating whole and half steps. It outlines a diminished-seventh chord from the tonic.
es.finger_use_it_over_7_harmony_diminished_: Use it over °7 harmony, diminished sequences and minor-third transposition practice.
es.finger_the_chromatic_scale_contains_all_: The chromatic scale contains all 12 pitch classes in the octave. It is not a major-scale mode but the complete semitone collection.
es.finger_use_it_for_technique_chromatic_ap: Use it for technique, chromatic approaches between chord tones, semitone ear training and chromatic line development.
es.finger_mixolydian_plus_a_major_7th_passi: Mixolydian plus a major 7th passing tone. With suitable rhythmic placement, chord tones can align consistently with strong beats.
es.finger_use_it_over_dominant_seventh_harm: Use it over dominant-seventh harmony in bebop and jazz; practise it rhythmically rather than only as a mechanical up-and-down scale.
es.finger_a_major_scale_with_a_lowered_6th_: A major scale with a lowered 6th, combining a major tonic with the ♭6 colour often associated with minor harmony.
es.finger_use_it_over_maj7_13_borrowed_harm: Use it over maj7(♭13), borrowed harmony and major-key lines requiring a darker colour.
es.finger_a_major_scale_with_2_and_6_creati: A major scale with ♭2 and ♭6, creating two characteristic augmented seconds. Some Western sources also call it Byzantine.
es.finger_use_it_for_western_labelled_middl: Use it for Western-labelled Middle Eastern/Mediterranean colours, metal, fusion and composition requiring strong tension.
es.finger_ritusen_yo_pentatonic_mode_12456_: Ritusen/Yo pentatonic mode: 1–2–4–5–6. With G as tonic, G–A–C–D–E shares the pitches of C major pentatonic, so its open C-reference shape is valid while G stays the root (R). This differs from dominant 1–3–4–5–b7.
es.finger_use_for_open_suspended_pentatonic: Use for open/suspended pentatonic sounds. In G, the C-major reference shape occupies open strings through fret 4; keep G as the tonal centre.
es.finger_tuner_tools_uses_the_common_weste: Tuner Tools uses the common Western reference form 1–2–♭3–5–♭6. Naming and pitches can vary with tuning, instrument and Japanese tradition.
es.finger_useful_for_pentatonic_melody_writ: Useful for pentatonic melody writing with wide gaps, a dark colour and interval-control practice.
es.finger_the_western_reference_form_12457_: The Western reference form 1–♭2–4–5–♭7 creates a dark suspended colour. Traditional terminology can vary by source and tuning.
es.finger_useful_over_sus_harmony_dark_melo: Useful over sus harmony, dark melody, ambient, metal and exercises emphasizing the ♭2.
es.finger_the_western_reference_form_12457_: The Western reference form 1–♭2–4–♭5–♭7 has strongly tense ♭2 and ♭5 degrees. Its historical name should not be treated as one absolutely fixed Western mode.
es.finger_useful_for_dark_melody_sound_desi: Useful for dark melody, sound design, metal and ear training with tense intervals.
es.finger_a_custom_roman_numeral_loop_that_: A custom Roman-numeral loop that is saved automatically and transposes to every key.
es.finger_the_dominant_of_the_target_chord_: The dominant of the target chord; its 3rd and 7th pull clearly into {0}.
es.finger_the_diminished_chord_root_lies_a_: The diminished chord root lies a semitone below {0}, resolving upward into the destination root.
es.finger_a_dominant_a_semitone_above_the_t: A dominant a semitone above the target, useful in jazz with a strong chromatic bass line.
es.finger_keep_the_hand_relaxed_and_play_1_: Keep the hand relaxed and play 1-2-3-4 evenly across six strings.
es.finger_each_finger_owns_one_fret_alterna: Each finger owns one fret; alternate picking synchronizes both hands.
es.finger_apply_the_same_pulse_to_a_short_c: Apply the same pulse to a short chromatic line.
es.finger_change_strings_without_breaking_t: Change strings without breaking the pulse and keep the picking motion compact.
es.finger_alternate_picking_continues_throu: Alternate picking continues through string changes instead of restarting on each string.
es.finger_use_this_motion_in_riffs_and_mult: Use this motion in riffs and multi-string solo lines.
es.finger_separate_each_finger_movement_esp: Separate each finger movement, especially fingers 3 and 4.
es.finger_lift_only_the_moving_finger_and_k: Lift only the moving finger and keep the others close to the strings.
es.finger_prepare_for_scale_and_arpeggio_li: Prepare for scale and arpeggio lines with changing finger order.
es.finger_keep_planted_fingers_down_while_t: Keep planted fingers down while the next finger crosses to the adjacent string.
es.finger_the_spider_drill_develops_finger_: The Spider drill develops finger independence and two-hand string control.
es.finger_useful_for_chords_legato_and_diag: Useful for chords, legato and diagonal string-crossing lines.
es.finger_keep_an_even_pulse_between_1_2_3_: Keep an even pulse between 1-2-3 and 2-3-4 groups.
es.finger_sequences_create_musical_phrasing: Sequences create musical phrasing instead of merely running straight up and down.
es.finger_use_three_note_groups_to_build_sc: Use three-note groups to build scale-based solo phrases.
es.finger_produce_even_notes_with_the_frett: Produce even notes with the fretting hand without repicking every note.
es.finger_pick_the_first_note_then_articula: Pick the first note, then articulate with the fretting hand while staying in time.
es.finger_apply_it_to_legato_phrases_and_po: Apply it to legato phrases and position connections.
es.finger_hear_and_see_the_root_third_and_f: Hear and see the root, third and fifth through an I-IV-V progression.
es.finger_the_third_defines_major_or_minor_: The third defines major or minor quality; the fifth adds stability.
es.finger_play_c_f_g_on_strings_1_2_3_with_: Play C-F-G on strings 1-2-3 with an even pulse.
es.finger_recognize_root_position_first_and: Recognize root position, first and second inversion in one fretboard area.
es.finger_the_lowest_note_determines_the_in: The lowest note determines the inversion while the three chord tones remain the same.
es.finger_connect_i_iv_v_with_the_nearest_i: Connect I-IV-V with the nearest inversion instead of large position jumps.
es.finger_triads_seven_chords_in_a_major_ke: Tríadas · siete acordes en modo mayor
es.finger_play_i_ii_iii_iv_v_vi_vii_and_rec: Play I-ii-iii-IV-V-vi-vii° and recognize root, first and second inversion on strings 1-2-3.
es.finger_in_every_major_key_the_seven_tria: In every major key, the seven triads follow: Major-Minor-Minor-Major-Major-Minor-Diminished.
es.finger_in_c_c_dm_em_f_g_am_bdim_this_map: In C: C-Dm-Em-F-G-Am-Bdim; this map supports accompaniment, analysis and progression building.
es.finger_connect_dm_g_c_with_minimal_hand_: Connect Dm-G-C with minimal hand movement.
es.finger_ii_prepares_v_creates_tension_and: ii prepares, V creates tension and I provides resolution.
es.finger_use_it_in_ballads_jazz_and_chord_: Use it in ballads, jazz and chord-tone soloing.
es.finger_connect_i_v_vi_iv_using_common_to: Connect I-V-vi-IV using common tones and nearest inversions.
es.finger_retaining_common_tones_smooths_ch: Retaining common tones smooths chord changes and reduces unnecessary motion.
es.finger_apply_it_directly_to_modern_pop_a: Apply it directly to modern pop and ballad accompaniment.
es.finger_seventh_chords_arpeggios_guide_to: Acordes de séptima · arpegios y notas guía
es.finger_play_dm7_g7_cmaj7_and_hear_the_co: Play Dm7-G7-Cmaj7 and hear the color of each seventh.
es.finger_the_third_and_seventh_are_guide_t: The third and seventh are guide tones that reveal harmonic function.
es.finger_resolve_phrases_to_the_third_or_s: Resolve phrases to the third or seventh over a ii-V-I.
es.finger_run_cmaj7_fmaj7_bm75_em7_am7_dm7_: Run Cmaj7-Fmaj7-Bm7♭5-Em7-Am7-Dm7-G7 and hear G7 resolve to Cmaj7.
es.finger_these_are_the_seven_diatonic_seve: These are the seven diatonic seventh chords of C major, ordered by fourths for function and voice-leading.

fr.finger_lesson_13_has_3_parts_13a_major_1: Lesson 13 has 3 parts: 13A Major → 13B Em7/E7 → 13C Minor
fr.finger_roots_on_strings_5_and_2_the_c_ma: Roots on strings 5 and 2; the C-major reference box spans frets 0-3
fr.finger_roots_on_strings_5_and_3_the_c_ma: Roots on strings 5 and 3; the C-major reference box spans frets 2-6
fr.finger_roots_on_strings_6_3_and_1_the_c_: Roots on strings 6, 3 and 1; the C-major reference box spans frets 5-8

fr.finger_roots_on_strings_4_and_2_the_c_ma: Roots on strings 4 and 2; the C-major reference box spans frets 9-13
fr.finger_ionian_is_the_standard_major_scal: Ionian is the standard major scale. Its major 7th creates a strong pull toward the tonic.
fr.finger_use_it_over_major_and_maj7_harmon: Use it over major and maj7 harmony and conventional major-key melodies.
fr.finger_dorian_is_a_minor_mode_with_a_nat: Dorian is a minor mode with a natural 6th, giving it a brighter sound than Aeolian.
fr.finger_useful_over_m7_and_m6_harmony_fun: Useful over m7 and m6 harmony, funk, jazz and Dorian vamps.
fr.finger_phrygian_is_a_minor_mode_whose_ch: Phrygian is a minor mode whose characteristic ♭2 creates a dark, tense pull near the tonic.
fr.finger_useful_over_static_minor_harmony_: Useful over static minor harmony, metal and Spanish-flavoured lines; it is not the same as Phrygian dominant.
fr.finger_lydian_is_a_major_mode_with_a_cha: Lydian is a major mode with a characteristic ♯4, producing a bright and open sound.
fr.finger_useful_over_maj7_and_maj711_harmo: Useful over maj7 and maj7♯11 harmony and modern, floating major sounds.
fr.finger_mixolydian_is_a_major_mode_with_a: Mixolydian is a major mode with a ♭7. The major 3rd and ♭7 clearly outline dominant function.
fr.finger_use_it_over_dominant_seventh_harm: Use it over dominant-seventh harmony, blues, rock, funk and Mixolydian progressions.
fr.finger_aeolian_is_the_natural_minor_scal: Aeolian is the natural minor scale. Its ♭6 is an important contrast with Dorian.
fr.finger_use_it_over_minor_harmony_natural: Use it over minor harmony, natural-minor progressions and stable, darker melodies.
fr.finger_locrian_is_a_minor_mode_with_a_5_: Locrian is a minor mode with a ♭5 and ♭2, so its tonic harmony is inherently unstable.
fr.finger_useful_over_m75_half_diminished_h: Useful over m7♭5 (half-diminished) harmony, ear training and highly tense passages.
fr.finger_harmonic_minor_raises_the_7th_of_: Harmonic minor raises the 7th of natural minor. The ♭6–7 span creates a strong pull to the tonic and its characteristic harmonic colour.
fr.finger_use_it_in_minor_key_harmony_espec: Use it in minor-key harmony, especially V7 resolving to i, as well as classical metal, neoclassical and many flamenco contexts.
fr.finger_this_is_the_jazz_melodic_minor_fo: This is the jazz melodic-minor form: the same collection ascending and descending. It can be heard as a major scale with a lowered 3rd.
fr.finger_use_it_over_m_maj7_and_m6_harmony: Use it over m(maj7) and m6 harmony and as the parent scale of Lydian dominant, Altered and the other melodic-minor modes.
fr.finger_a_bright_accessible_pentatonic_sc: A bright, accessible pentatonic scale with few avoid notes.
fr.finger_useful_for_pop_country_and_soloin: Useful for pop, country and soloing over major chords.
fr.finger_the_familiar_minor_pentatonic_sou: The familiar minor pentatonic sound used in blues and rock.
fr.finger_useful_for_blues_rock_and_soloing: Useful for blues, rock and soloing over minor chords.
fr.finger_a_variant_formed_by_omitting_degr: A variant formed by omitting degrees 2 and 6 from Mixolydian. “With 4” is shown because methods do not use one universal naming convention.
fr.finger_keeps_the_major_3rd_and_7_and_add: Keeps the major 3rd and ♭7 and adds the 4th; useful over dominant 7, 7sus4, funk and rock.
fr.finger_a_dominant_seventh_outline_plus_d: A dominant-seventh outline plus degree 2/9. Some methods also call it Mixolydian pentatonic.
fr.finger_useful_over_dominant_7_9_harmony_: Useful over dominant 7/9 harmony in jazz, blues and funk, especially when avoiding the 4th.
fr.finger_the_major_blues_scale_is_major_pe: The major blues scale is major pentatonic plus ♭3. The expressive tension between ♭3 and 3 creates its blues colour.
fr.finger_useful_for_major_blues_country_an: Useful for major blues, country and rock and roll over major or dominant harmony, treating ♭3 as a blue note.
fr.finger_the_minor_blues_scale_is_minor_pe: The minor blues scale is minor pentatonic plus ♭5. The ♭5 is its characteristic blue note, often approached or bent toward 5.
fr.finger_useful_for_blues_and_rock_over_mi: Useful for blues and rock over minor or dominant harmony, depending on the harmonic context.
fr.finger_the_second_mode_of_melodic_minor_: The second mode of melodic minor. It keeps Dorian's natural 6th while adding a dark, tense ♭2.
fr.finger_useful_over_m7_9_minor_sus_harmon: Useful over m7(♭9), minor-sus harmony and jazz/fusion passages requiring a darker Dorian colour.
fr.finger_the_third_mode_of_melodic_minor_c: The third mode of melodic minor, combining Lydian's ♯4 with the augmented chord's ♯5.
fr.finger_use_it_over_maj75_maj7115_and_mod: Use it over maj7♯5, maj7♯11♯5 and modern augmented-major harmony.
fr.finger_the_fourth_mode_of_melodic_minor_: The fourth mode of melodic minor, also called Lydian ♭7. It combines ♯4/♯11 with the dominant major 3rd and ♭7.
fr.finger_use_it_over_711_chords_non_resolv: Use it over 7♯11 chords, non-resolving dominants, jazz and fusion.
fr.finger_the_fifth_mode_of_melodic_minor_i: The fifth mode of melodic minor. It is Mixolydian with a ♭6, producing a darker dominant sound with a minor inflection.
fr.finger_use_it_over_7_13_dominants_resolv: Use it over 7(♭13), dominants resolving to minor and cinematic dominant harmony.
fr.finger_the_sixth_mode_of_melodic_minor_c: The sixth mode of melodic minor. Compared with ordinary Locrian, its natural 2nd softens the tension next to the tonic.
fr.finger_use_it_over_m75_when_a_natural_9_: Use it over m7♭5 when a natural 9 fits the harmony, especially in minor jazz ii–V–i progressions.
fr.finger_the_seventh_mode_of_melodic_minor: The seventh mode of melodic minor. Beyond 1, 3 and ♭7, it contains the altered dominant tensions ♭9, ♯9, ♭5/♯11 and ♭13.
fr.finger_use_it_over_7alt_79_79_75_or_713_: Use it over 7alt, 7♭9, 7♯9, 7♭5 or 7♭13 when a dominant chord requires strong resolution.
fr.finger_the_second_mode_of_harmonic_minor: The second mode of harmonic minor. It keeps Locrian's ♭2 and ♭5 while raising ♭6 to a natural 6th.
fr.finger_use_it_over_m75_when_a_natural_13: Use it over m7♭5 when a natural 13 fits, or for a brighter half-diminished colour than ordinary Locrian.
fr.finger_the_third_mode_of_harmonic_minor_: The third mode of harmonic minor. It is Ionian with a ♯5, creating a maj7♯5 tonic while retaining a natural 4th.
fr.finger_use_it_over_maj75_and_augmented_m: Use it over maj7♯5 and augmented-major harmony when the natural 4th is preferred to Lydian augmented's ♯4.
fr.finger_the_fourth_mode_of_harmonic_minor: The fourth mode of harmonic minor. It keeps Dorian's natural 6th while replacing the natural 4th with ♯4.
fr.finger_use_it_over_m711_fusion_metal_and: Use it over m7♯11, fusion, metal and minor vamps requiring a brighter yet tenser colour than ordinary Dorian.
fr.finger_the_fifth_mode_of_harmonic_minor_: The fifth mode of harmonic minor. Its ♭2 combined with a major 3rd creates a distinctive dominant sound unlike ordinary Phrygian.
fr.finger_use_it_over_v7_in_minor_keys_9_13: Use it over V7 in minor keys, ♭9/♭13 dominants, metal, fusion and many flamenco contexts.
fr.finger_the_sixth_mode_of_harmonic_minor_: The sixth mode of harmonic minor. It combines ♯2 with Lydian's ♯4, creating an augmented second near the tonic.
fr.finger_use_it_over_maj711_when_a_9_2_fit: Use it over maj7♯11 when a ♯9/♯2 fits the line, mainly in advanced composition and jazz contexts.
fr.finger_the_seventh_mode_of_harmonic_mino: The seventh mode of harmonic minor. It is highly tense, with ♭4, ♭5 and a doubly lowered 7th; it is not the melodic-minor Altered/Super Locrian scale.
fr.finger_use_sparingly_in_composition_dimi: Use sparingly in composition, diminished/altered harmony and advanced ear training; always read it together with its formula.
fr.finger_a_six_note_scale_built_entirely_f: A six-note scale built entirely from whole steps. With no semitones, it sounds floating and unresolved.
fr.finger_use_it_over_augmented_harmony_and: Use it over augmented harmony and dominant chords with ♯5/♭5 for an ambiguous, symmetrical colour.
fr.finger_an_eight_note_symmetrical_scale_a: An eight-note symmetrical scale alternating half and whole steps. It contains a dominant chord plus several altered tensions.
fr.finger_use_it_over_79_79_139_and_dominan: Use it over 7♭9, 7♯9, 13♭9 and dominant-diminished harmony, especially before resolution.
fr.finger_an_eight_note_symmetrical_scale_a: An eight-note symmetrical scale alternating whole and half steps. It outlines a diminished-seventh chord from the tonic.
fr.finger_use_it_over_7_harmony_diminished_: Use it over °7 harmony, diminished sequences and minor-third transposition practice.
fr.finger_the_chromatic_scale_contains_all_: The chromatic scale contains all 12 pitch classes in the octave. It is not a major-scale mode but the complete semitone collection.
fr.finger_use_it_for_technique_chromatic_ap: Use it for technique, chromatic approaches between chord tones, semitone ear training and chromatic line development.
fr.finger_mixolydian_plus_a_major_7th_passi: Mixolydian plus a major 7th passing tone. With suitable rhythmic placement, chord tones can align consistently with strong beats.
fr.finger_use_it_over_dominant_seventh_harm: Use it over dominant-seventh harmony in bebop and jazz; practise it rhythmically rather than only as a mechanical up-and-down scale.
fr.finger_a_major_scale_with_a_lowered_6th_: A major scale with a lowered 6th, combining a major tonic with the ♭6 colour often associated with minor harmony.
fr.finger_use_it_over_maj7_13_borrowed_harm: Use it over maj7(♭13), borrowed harmony and major-key lines requiring a darker colour.
fr.finger_a_major_scale_with_2_and_6_creati: A major scale with ♭2 and ♭6, creating two characteristic augmented seconds. Some Western sources also call it Byzantine.
fr.finger_use_it_for_western_labelled_middl: Use it for Western-labelled Middle Eastern/Mediterranean colours, metal, fusion and composition requiring strong tension.
fr.finger_ritusen_yo_pentatonic_mode_12456_: Ritusen/Yo pentatonic mode: 1–2–4–5–6. With G as tonic, G–A–C–D–E shares the pitches of C major pentatonic, so its open C-reference shape is valid while G stays the root (R). This differs from dominant 1–3–4–5–b7.
fr.finger_use_for_open_suspended_pentatonic: Use for open/suspended pentatonic sounds. In G, the C-major reference shape occupies open strings through fret 4; keep G as the tonal centre.
fr.finger_tuner_tools_uses_the_common_weste: Tuner Tools uses the common Western reference form 1–2–♭3–5–♭6. Naming and pitches can vary with tuning, instrument and Japanese tradition.
fr.finger_useful_for_pentatonic_melody_writ: Useful for pentatonic melody writing with wide gaps, a dark colour and interval-control practice.
fr.finger_the_western_reference_form_12457_: The Western reference form 1–♭2–4–5–♭7 creates a dark suspended colour. Traditional terminology can vary by source and tuning.
fr.finger_useful_over_sus_harmony_dark_melo: Useful over sus harmony, dark melody, ambient, metal and exercises emphasizing the ♭2.
fr.finger_the_western_reference_form_12457_: The Western reference form 1–♭2–4–♭5–♭7 has strongly tense ♭2 and ♭5 degrees. Its historical name should not be treated as one absolutely fixed Western mode.
fr.finger_useful_for_dark_melody_sound_desi: Useful for dark melody, sound design, metal and ear training with tense intervals.

de.finger_roots_on_strings_5_and_2_the_c_ma: Roots on strings 5 and 2; the C-major reference box spans frets 0-3
de.finger_roots_on_strings_5_and_3_the_c_ma: Roots on strings 5 and 3; the C-major reference box spans frets 2-6
de.finger_roots_on_strings_6_3_and_1_the_c_: Roots on strings 6, 3 and 1; the C-major reference box spans frets 5-8
de.finger_roots_on_strings_6_4_and_1_the_c_: Roots on strings 6, 4 and 1; the C-major reference box spans frets 7-10

de.finger_ionian_is_the_standard_major_scal: Ionian is the standard major scale. Its major 7th creates a strong pull toward the tonic.
de.finger_use_it_over_major_and_maj7_harmon: Use it over major and maj7 harmony and conventional major-key melodies.
de.finger_dorian_is_a_minor_mode_with_a_nat: Dorian is a minor mode with a natural 6th, giving it a brighter sound than Aeolian.
de.finger_useful_over_m7_and_m6_harmony_fun: Useful over m7 and m6 harmony, funk, jazz and Dorian vamps.
de.finger_phrygian_is_a_minor_mode_whose_ch: Phrygian is a minor mode whose characteristic ♭2 creates a dark, tense pull near the tonic.
de.finger_useful_over_static_minor_harmony_: Useful over static minor harmony, metal and Spanish-flavoured lines; it is not the same as Phrygian dominant.
de.finger_lydian_is_a_major_mode_with_a_cha: Lydian is a major mode with a characteristic ♯4, producing a bright and open sound.
de.finger_useful_over_maj7_and_maj711_harmo: Useful over maj7 and maj7♯11 harmony and modern, floating major sounds.
de.finger_mixolydian_is_a_major_mode_with_a: Mixolydian is a major mode with a ♭7. The major 3rd and ♭7 clearly outline dominant function.
de.finger_use_it_over_dominant_seventh_harm: Use it over dominant-seventh harmony, blues, rock, funk and Mixolydian progressions.
de.finger_aeolian_is_the_natural_minor_scal: Aeolian is the natural minor scale. Its ♭6 is an important contrast with Dorian.
de.finger_use_it_over_minor_harmony_natural: Use it over minor harmony, natural-minor progressions and stable, darker melodies.
de.finger_locrian_is_a_minor_mode_with_a_5_: Locrian is a minor mode with a ♭5 and ♭2, so its tonic harmony is inherently unstable.
de.finger_useful_over_m75_half_diminished_h: Useful over m7♭5 (half-diminished) harmony, ear training and highly tense passages.
de.finger_harmonic_minor_raises_the_7th_of_: Harmonic minor raises the 7th of natural minor. The ♭6–7 span creates a strong pull to the tonic and its characteristic harmonic colour.
de.finger_use_it_in_minor_key_harmony_espec: Use it in minor-key harmony, especially V7 resolving to i, as well as classical metal, neoclassical and many flamenco contexts.
de.finger_this_is_the_jazz_melodic_minor_fo: This is the jazz melodic-minor form: the same collection ascending and descending. It can be heard as a major scale with a lowered 3rd.
de.finger_use_it_over_m_maj7_and_m6_harmony: Use it over m(maj7) and m6 harmony and as the parent scale of Lydian dominant, Altered and the other melodic-minor modes.
de.finger_a_bright_accessible_pentatonic_sc: A bright, accessible pentatonic scale with few avoid notes.
de.finger_useful_for_pop_country_and_soloin: Useful for pop, country and soloing over major chords.
de.finger_the_familiar_minor_pentatonic_sou: The familiar minor pentatonic sound used in blues and rock.
de.finger_useful_for_blues_rock_and_soloing: Useful for blues, rock and soloing over minor chords.
de.finger_a_variant_formed_by_omitting_degr: A variant formed by omitting degrees 2 and 6 from Mixolydian. “With 4” is shown because methods do not use one universal naming convention.
de.finger_keeps_the_major_3rd_and_7_and_add: Keeps the major 3rd and ♭7 and adds the 4th; useful over dominant 7, 7sus4, funk and rock.
de.finger_a_dominant_seventh_outline_plus_d: A dominant-seventh outline plus degree 2/9. Some methods also call it Mixolydian pentatonic.
de.finger_useful_over_dominant_7_9_harmony_: Useful over dominant 7/9 harmony in jazz, blues and funk, especially when avoiding the 4th.
de.finger_the_major_blues_scale_is_major_pe: The major blues scale is major pentatonic plus ♭3. The expressive tension between ♭3 and 3 creates its blues colour.
de.finger_useful_for_major_blues_country_an: Useful for major blues, country and rock and roll over major or dominant harmony, treating ♭3 as a blue note.
de.finger_the_minor_blues_scale_is_minor_pe: The minor blues scale is minor pentatonic plus ♭5. The ♭5 is its characteristic blue note, often approached or bent toward 5.
de.finger_useful_for_blues_and_rock_over_mi: Useful for blues and rock over minor or dominant harmony, depending on the harmonic context.
de.finger_the_second_mode_of_melodic_minor_: The second mode of melodic minor. It keeps Dorian's natural 6th while adding a dark, tense ♭2.
de.finger_useful_over_m7_9_minor_sus_harmon: Useful over m7(♭9), minor-sus harmony and jazz/fusion passages requiring a darker Dorian colour.
de.finger_the_third_mode_of_melodic_minor_c: The third mode of melodic minor, combining Lydian's ♯4 with the augmented chord's ♯5.
de.finger_use_it_over_maj75_maj7115_and_mod: Use it over maj7♯5, maj7♯11♯5 and modern augmented-major harmony.
de.finger_the_fourth_mode_of_melodic_minor_: The fourth mode of melodic minor, also called Lydian ♭7. It combines ♯4/♯11 with the dominant major 3rd and ♭7.
de.finger_use_it_over_711_chords_non_resolv: Use it over 7♯11 chords, non-resolving dominants, jazz and fusion.
de.finger_the_fifth_mode_of_melodic_minor_i: The fifth mode of melodic minor. It is Mixolydian with a ♭6, producing a darker dominant sound with a minor inflection.
de.finger_use_it_over_7_13_dominants_resolv: Use it over 7(♭13), dominants resolving to minor and cinematic dominant harmony.
de.finger_the_sixth_mode_of_melodic_minor_c: The sixth mode of melodic minor. Compared with ordinary Locrian, its natural 2nd softens the tension next to the tonic.
de.finger_use_it_over_m75_when_a_natural_9_: Use it over m7♭5 when a natural 9 fits the harmony, especially in minor jazz ii–V–i progressions.
de.finger_the_seventh_mode_of_melodic_minor: The seventh mode of melodic minor. Beyond 1, 3 and ♭7, it contains the altered dominant tensions ♭9, ♯9, ♭5/♯11 and ♭13.
de.finger_use_it_over_7alt_79_79_75_or_713_: Use it over 7alt, 7♭9, 7♯9, 7♭5 or 7♭13 when a dominant chord requires strong resolution.
de.finger_the_second_mode_of_harmonic_minor: The second mode of harmonic minor. It keeps Locrian's ♭2 and ♭5 while raising ♭6 to a natural 6th.
de.finger_use_it_over_m75_when_a_natural_13: Use it over m7♭5 when a natural 13 fits, or for a brighter half-diminished colour than ordinary Locrian.
de.finger_the_third_mode_of_harmonic_minor_: The third mode of harmonic minor. It is Ionian with a ♯5, creating a maj7♯5 tonic while retaining a natural 4th.
de.finger_use_it_over_maj75_and_augmented_m: Use it over maj7♯5 and augmented-major harmony when the natural 4th is preferred to Lydian augmented's ♯4.
de.finger_the_fourth_mode_of_harmonic_minor: The fourth mode of harmonic minor. It keeps Dorian's natural 6th while replacing the natural 4th with ♯4.
de.finger_use_it_over_m711_fusion_metal_and: Use it over m7♯11, fusion, metal and minor vamps requiring a brighter yet tenser colour than ordinary Dorian.
de.finger_the_fifth_mode_of_harmonic_minor_: The fifth mode of harmonic minor. Its ♭2 combined with a major 3rd creates a distinctive dominant sound unlike ordinary Phrygian.
de.finger_use_it_over_v7_in_minor_keys_9_13: Use it over V7 in minor keys, ♭9/♭13 dominants, metal, fusion and many flamenco contexts.
de.finger_the_sixth_mode_of_harmonic_minor_: The sixth mode of harmonic minor. It combines ♯2 with Lydian's ♯4, creating an augmented second near the tonic.
de.finger_use_it_over_maj711_when_a_9_2_fit: Use it over maj7♯11 when a ♯9/♯2 fits the line, mainly in advanced composition and jazz contexts.
de.finger_the_seventh_mode_of_harmonic_mino: The seventh mode of harmonic minor. It is highly tense, with ♭4, ♭5 and a doubly lowered 7th; it is not the melodic-minor Altered/Super Locrian scale.
de.finger_use_sparingly_in_composition_dimi: Use sparingly in composition, diminished/altered harmony and advanced ear training; always read it together with its formula.
de.finger_a_six_note_scale_built_entirely_f: A six-note scale built entirely from whole steps. With no semitones, it sounds floating and unresolved.
de.finger_use_it_over_augmented_harmony_and: Use it over augmented harmony and dominant chords with ♯5/♭5 for an ambiguous, symmetrical colour.
de.finger_an_eight_note_symmetrical_scale_a: An eight-note symmetrical scale alternating half and whole steps. It contains a dominant chord plus several altered tensions.
de.finger_use_it_over_79_79_139_and_dominan: Use it over 7♭9, 7♯9, 13♭9 and dominant-diminished harmony, especially before resolution.
de.finger_an_eight_note_symmetrical_scale_a: An eight-note symmetrical scale alternating whole and half steps. It outlines a diminished-seventh chord from the tonic.
de.finger_use_it_over_7_harmony_diminished_: Use it over °7 harmony, diminished sequences and minor-third transposition practice.
de.finger_the_chromatic_scale_contains_all_: The chromatic scale contains all 12 pitch classes in the octave. It is not a major-scale mode but the complete semitone collection.
de.finger_use_it_for_technique_chromatic_ap: Use it for technique, chromatic approaches between chord tones, semitone ear training and chromatic line development.
de.finger_mixolydian_plus_a_major_7th_passi: Mixolydian plus a major 7th passing tone. With suitable rhythmic placement, chord tones can align consistently with strong beats.
de.finger_use_it_over_dominant_seventh_harm: Use it over dominant-seventh harmony in bebop and jazz; practise it rhythmically rather than only as a mechanical up-and-down scale.
de.finger_a_major_scale_with_a_lowered_6th_: A major scale with a lowered 6th, combining a major tonic with the ♭6 colour often associated with minor harmony.
de.finger_use_it_over_maj7_13_borrowed_harm: Use it over maj7(♭13), borrowed harmony and major-key lines requiring a darker colour.
de.finger_a_major_scale_with_2_and_6_creati: A major scale with ♭2 and ♭6, creating two characteristic augmented seconds. Some Western sources also call it Byzantine.
de.finger_use_it_for_western_labelled_middl: Use it for Western-labelled Middle Eastern/Mediterranean colours, metal, fusion and composition requiring strong tension.
de.finger_ritusen_yo_pentatonic_mode_12456_: Ritusen/Yo pentatonic mode: 1–2–4–5–6. With G as tonic, G–A–C–D–E shares the pitches of C major pentatonic, so its open C-reference shape is valid while G stays the root (R). This differs from dominant 1–3–4–5–b7.
de.finger_use_for_open_suspended_pentatonic: Use for open/suspended pentatonic sounds. In G, the C-major reference shape occupies open strings through fret 4; keep G as the tonal centre.
de.finger_tuner_tools_uses_the_common_weste: Tuner Tools uses the common Western reference form 1–2–♭3–5–♭6. Naming and pitches can vary with tuning, instrument and Japanese tradition.
de.finger_useful_for_pentatonic_melody_writ: Useful for pentatonic melody writing with wide gaps, a dark colour and interval-control practice.
de.finger_the_western_reference_form_12457_: The Western reference form 1–♭2–4–5–♭7 creates a dark suspended colour. Traditional terminology can vary by source and tuning.
de.finger_useful_over_sus_harmony_dark_melo: Useful over sus harmony, dark melody, ambient, metal and exercises emphasizing the ♭2.
de.finger_the_western_reference_form_12457_: The Western reference form 1–♭2–4–♭5–♭7 has strongly tense ♭2 and ♭5 degrees. Its historical name should not be treated as one absolutely fixed Western mode.
de.finger_useful_for_dark_melody_sound_desi: Useful for dark melody, sound design, metal and ear training with tense intervals.
de.finger_a_custom_roman_numeral_loop_that_: A custom Roman-numeral loop that is saved automatically and transposes to every key.
de.finger_the_dominant_of_the_target_chord_: The dominant of the target chord; its 3rd and 7th pull clearly into {0}.
de.finger_the_diminished_chord_root_lies_a_: The diminished chord root lies a semitone below {0}, resolving upward into the destination root.
de.finger_a_dominant_a_semitone_above_the_t: A dominant a semitone above the target, useful in jazz with a strong chromatic bass line.
de.finger_keep_the_hand_relaxed_and_play_1_: Keep the hand relaxed and play 1-2-3-4 evenly across six strings.
de.finger_each_finger_owns_one_fret_alterna: Each finger owns one fret; alternate picking synchronizes both hands.
de.finger_apply_the_same_pulse_to_a_short_c: Apply the same pulse to a short chromatic line.
de.finger_change_strings_without_breaking_t: Change strings without breaking the pulse and keep the picking motion compact.
de.finger_alternate_picking_continues_throu: Alternate picking continues through string changes instead of restarting on each string.
de.finger_use_this_motion_in_riffs_and_mult: Use this motion in riffs and multi-string solo lines.
de.finger_separate_each_finger_movement_esp: Separate each finger movement, especially fingers 3 and 4.
de.finger_lift_only_the_moving_finger_and_k: Lift only the moving finger and keep the others close to the strings.
de.finger_prepare_for_scale_and_arpeggio_li: Prepare for scale and arpeggio lines with changing finger order.
de.finger_keep_planted_fingers_down_while_t: Keep planted fingers down while the next finger crosses to the adjacent string.
de.finger_the_spider_drill_develops_finger_: The Spider drill develops finger independence and two-hand string control.
de.finger_useful_for_chords_legato_and_diag: Useful for chords, legato and diagonal string-crossing lines.
de.finger_keep_an_even_pulse_between_1_2_3_: Keep an even pulse between 1-2-3 and 2-3-4 groups.
de.finger_sequences_create_musical_phrasing: Sequences create musical phrasing instead of merely running straight up and down.
de.finger_use_three_note_groups_to_build_sc: Use three-note groups to build scale-based solo phrases.
de.finger_produce_even_notes_with_the_frett: Produce even notes with the fretting hand without repicking every note.
de.finger_pick_the_first_note_then_articula: Pick the first note, then articulate with the fretting hand while staying in time.
de.finger_apply_it_to_legato_phrases_and_po: Apply it to legato phrases and position connections.
de.finger_hear_and_see_the_root_third_and_f: Hear and see the root, third and fifth through an I-IV-V progression.
de.finger_the_third_defines_major_or_minor_: The third defines major or minor quality; the fifth adds stability.
de.finger_play_c_f_g_on_strings_1_2_3_with_: Play C-F-G on strings 1-2-3 with an even pulse.
de.finger_recognize_root_position_first_and: Recognize root position, first and second inversion in one fretboard area.
de.finger_the_lowest_note_determines_the_in: The lowest note determines the inversion while the three chord tones remain the same.
de.finger_connect_i_iv_v_with_the_nearest_i: Connect I-IV-V with the nearest inversion instead of large position jumps.
de.finger_play_i_ii_iii_iv_v_vi_vii_and_rec: Play I-ii-iii-IV-V-vi-vii° and recognize root, first and second inversion on strings 1-2-3.
de.finger_in_every_major_key_the_seven_tria: In every major key, the seven triads follow: Major-Minor-Minor-Major-Major-Minor-Diminished.
de.finger_in_c_c_dm_em_f_g_am_bdim_this_map: In C: C-Dm-Em-F-G-Am-Bdim; this map supports accompaniment, analysis and progression building.
de.finger_connect_dm_g_c_with_minimal_hand_: Connect Dm-G-C with minimal hand movement.
de.finger_ii_prepares_v_creates_tension_and: ii prepares, V creates tension and I provides resolution.
de.finger_use_it_in_ballads_jazz_and_chord_: Use it in ballads, jazz and chord-tone soloing.
de.finger_connect_i_v_vi_iv_using_common_to: Connect I-V-vi-IV using common tones and nearest inversions.
de.finger_retaining_common_tones_smooths_ch: Retaining common tones smooths chord changes and reduces unnecessary motion.
de.finger_apply_it_directly_to_modern_pop_a: Apply it directly to modern pop and ballad accompaniment.
de.finger_play_dm7_g7_cmaj7_and_hear_the_co: Play Dm7-G7-Cmaj7 and hear the color of each seventh.
de.finger_the_third_and_seventh_are_guide_t: The third and seventh are guide tones that reveal harmonic function.
de.finger_resolve_phrases_to_the_third_or_s: Resolve phrases to the third or seventh over a ii-V-I.
de.finger_run_cmaj7_fmaj7_bm75_em7_am7_dm7_: Run Cmaj7-Fmaj7-Bm7♭5-Em7-Am7-Dm7-G7 and hear G7 resolve to Cmaj7.
de.finger_these_are_the_seven_diatonic_seve: These are the seven diatonic seventh chords of C major, ordered by fourths for function and voice-leading.
de.finger_use_this_cycle_for_harmonic_analy: Use this cycle for harmonic analysis, guide-tone practice and smooth jazz/pop changes.
de.finger_compare_em7am7_with_e7am7_and_hea: Compare Em7→Am7 with E7→Am7 and hear G rise to G#, creating a pull toward A.
de.finger_em7_belongs_to_a_natural_minor_e7: Em7 belongs to A natural minor; E7 borrows G# from A harmonic minor to become the dominant V7.
de.finger_hear_and_see_both_resolutions_to_: Hear and see both resolutions to understand why E7→Am is stronger than Em7→Am.
de.finger_combine_seventh_chord_arpeggios_v: Combine seventh-chord arpeggios, voice-leading and harmonic minor through Am7-Dm7-G7-Cmaj7-Fmaj7-Bm7♭5-E7.
de.finger_e7_uses_g_from_harmonic_minor_to_: E7 uses G# from harmonic minor to pull strongly back to Am.
de.finger_apply_it_to_jazz_turnarounds_stan: Apply it to jazz turnarounds, standards and key movement.
de.finger_scale_order_i_ii_iii_iv_v_vi_vii_: Scale order I-ii-iii-IV-V-vi-vii°: C-Dm-Em-F-G-Am-Bdim in C major.
de.finger_diatonic_1473625_cfbdimemamdmg_in: Diatonic 1–4–7–3–6–2–5: C–F–Bdim–Em–Am–Dm–G in C; resolves to I.
de.finger_a_minor_compare_em7am7_natural_mi: A minor: compare Em7→Am7 (natural minor) with E7→Am7 (harmonic minor, G# leading to A).
de.finger_the_classic_jazz_cadence_for_targ: The classic jazz cadence for target notes and harmonic resolution.
de.finger_a_foundation_of_pop_rock_blues_an: A foundation of pop, rock, blues and folk.
de.finger_a_modern_pop_ballad_loop_ideal_fo: A modern pop/ballad loop ideal for connected positions.
de.finger_a_common_turnaround_in_jazz_balla: A common turnaround in jazz, ballads and standards.
de.finger_the_classic_1_6_4_5_loop_for_acco: The classic 1-6-4-5 loop for accompaniment and chord changes.
de.finger_a_minor_2_5_1_with_half_diminishe: A minor 2-5-1 with half-diminished ii and a strong V7 pull.
de.finger_a_familiar_minor_key_loop_in_rock: A familiar minor-key loop in rock, pop and cinematic music.
de.finger_a_basic_minor_functional_cadence_: A basic minor functional cadence with a major V resolving to i.
de.finger_twelve_bars_of_i7_iv7_v7_for_groo: Twelve bars of I7-IV7-V7 for groove and dominant arpeggios.
de.finger_pattern_1_2_3_4_on_each_string_re: Muster 1-2-3-4 auf jeder Saite · ideal zum Einstieg
de.finger_starts_at_frets_14_choose_frets_5: Beginnt bei Bund 1–4; bei unbequemer Dehnung 5–8 wählen.
de.finger_move_only_the_required_finger_wit: Nur den benötigten Finger bewegen, nicht die ganze Hand.
de.finger_the_spider_exercise_moves_diagona: Spider-Übung wechselt diagonal zwischen benachbarten Saiten
de.finger_keep_planted_fingers_down_and_mov: Aufgesetzte Finger liegen lassen, nur den nächsten bewegen.
de.finger_play_continuous_1_2_3_and_2_3_4_g: Gruppen 1-2-3 und 2-3-4 auf jeder Saite durchgehend spielen
de.finger_keep_an_even_pulse_between_the_1_: Keep an even pulse between the 1-2-3 and 2-3-4 groups.
de.finger_a_left_hand_technique_for_after_t: Technik der linken Hand nach Beherrschung der vier Finger
de.finger_pick_the_first_note_then_use_the_: Pick the first note, then use the fretting hand while keeping steady time.
de.finger_plant_one_or_two_fingers_move_the: Ein oder zwei Finger festhalten und die anderen auf einer Saite bewegen
de.finger_keep_the_anchored_fingers_down_ch: Fixierte Finger liegen lassen. Einen oder zwei wählen, langsam und locker spielen.
de.finger_anchor_one_or_two_fingers_move_th: Ein oder zwei Finger halten, die übrigen zwischen zwei Saiten bewegen
de.finger_plant_the_anchors_on_separate_str: Fixierte Finger auf getrennten Saiten halten, andere kreuzen benachbarte Saiten.
de.finger_seven_modes_of_the_major_scale_5d: Seven modes of the major scale
de.finger_six_core_drills_plus_two_held_fin: Six core drills plus two held-finger variants (straight/cross-string). Open 'Hand positions' for CAGED.
de.finger_the_caged_position_system_is_arra: The CAGED position system is arranged for a six-string guitar fretboard.
de.finger_tonic_0_caged_shapes_refer_to_1_m: Tonic {0} · CAGED shapes refer to {1} major pentatonic. The tonic does not change when switching shapes.
de.finger_harmony_colours_are_calculated_ag: Harmony colours are calculated against the tonic triad: blue marks chord tones; green marks the remaining matching pentatonic tones; gold marks colour tensions; red marks strong tensions that commonly resolve to a nearby tone. In A Aeolian over Am: A–C–E are blue, D–G green, B gold and F red.
de.finger_3nps_requires_a_seven_tone_scale_: 3NPS requires a seven-tone scale. Choose a major mode, harmonic minor or melodic minor. Pentatonic and blues scales stay in CAGED.
de.finger_keep_0_as_tonic_r_1_only_locates_: Keep {0} as tonic (R). {1} only locates the CAGED shape; changing shapes does not change the scale.
de.finger_each_string_contains_three_scale_: Each string contains three scale tones; play from low E (6) to high E (1). Circles show scale degrees, not finger numbers.

de.finger_red_tonic_teal_fifth_other_colors: ● Red: tonic  ·  ● Teal: fifth  ·  ● Other colors: scale degrees

de.finger_compare_scale_degrees_and_practis: Compare scale degrees and practise the notes.
de.finger_move_through_c_a_g_e_d_with_the_s: Move through C – A – G – E – D with the same note set.
de.finger_explore_chord_shapes_and_fretboar: Explore chord shapes and fretboard positions.

de.finger_explore_connected_positions_along: Explore connected positions along the fretboard.

de.finger_this_lesson_requires_the_supporte: Für diese Lektion ist ein unterstütztes Instrument nötig.

de.finger_follow_0_goal_based_lessons_or_bu: Follow {0} goal-based lessons or build your own practice session.
de.finger_practice_six_finger_drills_and_fi: Übe sechs Fingerübungen und fünf CAGED-Positionen auf dem Griffbrett.

ru.finger_lesson_13_has_3_parts_13a_major_1: Lesson 13 has 3 parts: 13A Major → 13B Em7/E7 → 13C Minor
ru.finger_roots_on_strings_5_and_2_the_c_ma: Roots on strings 5 and 2; the C-major reference box spans frets 0-3
ru.finger_roots_on_strings_5_and_3_the_c_ma: Roots on strings 5 and 3; the C-major reference box spans frets 2-6
ru.finger_roots_on_strings_6_3_and_1_the_c_: Roots on strings 6, 3 and 1; the C-major reference box spans frets 5-8
ru.finger_roots_on_strings_6_4_and_1_the_c_: Roots on strings 6, 4 and 1; the C-major reference box spans frets 7-10
ru.finger_roots_on_strings_4_and_2_the_c_ma: Roots on strings 4 and 2; the C-major reference box spans frets 9-13
ru.finger_ionian_is_the_standard_major_scal: Ionian is the standard major scale. Its major 7th creates a strong pull toward the tonic.
ru.finger_use_it_over_major_and_maj7_harmon: Use it over major and maj7 harmony and conventional major-key melodies.
ru.finger_dorian_is_a_minor_mode_with_a_nat: Dorian is a minor mode with a natural 6th, giving it a brighter sound than Aeolian.
ru.finger_useful_over_m7_and_m6_harmony_fun: Useful over m7 and m6 harmony, funk, jazz and Dorian vamps.
ru.finger_phrygian_is_a_minor_mode_whose_ch: Phrygian is a minor mode whose characteristic ♭2 creates a dark, tense pull near the tonic.
ru.finger_useful_over_static_minor_harmony_: Useful over static minor harmony, metal and Spanish-flavoured lines; it is not the same as Phrygian dominant.
ru.finger_lydian_is_a_major_mode_with_a_cha: Lydian is a major mode with a characteristic ♯4, producing a bright and open sound.
ru.finger_useful_over_maj7_and_maj711_harmo: Useful over maj7 and maj7♯11 harmony and modern, floating major sounds.
ru.finger_mixolydian_is_a_major_mode_with_a: Mixolydian is a major mode with a ♭7. The major 3rd and ♭7 clearly outline dominant function.
ru.finger_use_it_over_dominant_seventh_harm: Use it over dominant-seventh harmony, blues, rock, funk and Mixolydian progressions.
ru.finger_aeolian_is_the_natural_minor_scal: Aeolian is the natural minor scale. Its ♭6 is an important contrast with Dorian.
ru.finger_use_it_over_minor_harmony_natural: Use it over minor harmony, natural-minor progressions and stable, darker melodies.
ru.finger_locrian_is_a_minor_mode_with_a_5_: Locrian is a minor mode with a ♭5 and ♭2, so its tonic harmony is inherently unstable.
ru.finger_useful_over_m75_half_diminished_h: Useful over m7♭5 (half-diminished) harmony, ear training and highly tense passages.
ru.finger_harmonic_minor_raises_the_7th_of_: Harmonic minor raises the 7th of natural minor. The ♭6–7 span creates a strong pull to the tonic and its characteristic harmonic colour.
ru.finger_use_it_in_minor_key_harmony_espec: Use it in minor-key harmony, especially V7 resolving to i, as well as classical metal, neoclassical and many flamenco contexts.
ru.finger_this_is_the_jazz_melodic_minor_fo: This is the jazz melodic-minor form: the same collection ascending and descending. It can be heard as a major scale with a lowered 3rd.
ru.finger_use_it_over_m_maj7_and_m6_harmony: Use it over m(maj7) and m6 harmony and as the parent scale of Lydian dominant, Altered and the other melodic-minor modes.
ru.finger_a_bright_accessible_pentatonic_sc: A bright, accessible pentatonic scale with few avoid notes.
ru.finger_useful_for_pop_country_and_soloin: Useful for pop, country and soloing over major chords.
ru.finger_the_familiar_minor_pentatonic_sou: The familiar minor pentatonic sound used in blues and rock.
ru.finger_useful_for_blues_rock_and_soloing: Useful for blues, rock and soloing over minor chords.
ru.finger_a_variant_formed_by_omitting_degr: A variant formed by omitting degrees 2 and 6 from Mixolydian. “With 4” is shown because methods do not use one universal naming convention.
ru.finger_keeps_the_major_3rd_and_7_and_add: Keeps the major 3rd and ♭7 and adds the 4th; useful over dominant 7, 7sus4, funk and rock.
ru.finger_a_dominant_seventh_outline_plus_d: A dominant-seventh outline plus degree 2/9. Some methods also call it Mixolydian pentatonic.
ru.finger_useful_over_dominant_7_9_harmony_: Useful over dominant 7/9 harmony in jazz, blues and funk, especially when avoiding the 4th.
ru.finger_the_major_blues_scale_is_major_pe: The major blues scale is major pentatonic plus ♭3. The expressive tension between ♭3 and 3 creates its blues colour.
ru.finger_useful_for_major_blues_country_an: Useful for major blues, country and rock and roll over major or dominant harmony, treating ♭3 as a blue note.
ru.finger_the_minor_blues_scale_is_minor_pe: The minor blues scale is minor pentatonic plus ♭5. The ♭5 is its characteristic blue note, often approached or bent toward 5.
ru.finger_useful_for_blues_and_rock_over_mi: Useful for blues and rock over minor or dominant harmony, depending on the harmonic context.
ru.finger_the_second_mode_of_melodic_minor_: The second mode of melodic minor. It keeps Dorian's natural 6th while adding a dark, tense ♭2.
ru.finger_useful_over_m7_9_minor_sus_harmon: Useful over m7(♭9), minor-sus harmony and jazz/fusion passages requiring a darker Dorian colour.
ru.finger_the_third_mode_of_melodic_minor_c: The third mode of melodic minor, combining Lydian's ♯4 with the augmented chord's ♯5.
ru.finger_use_it_over_maj75_maj7115_and_mod: Use it over maj7♯5, maj7♯11♯5 and modern augmented-major harmony.
ru.finger_the_fourth_mode_of_melodic_minor_: The fourth mode of melodic minor, also called Lydian ♭7. It combines ♯4/♯11 with the dominant major 3rd and ♭7.
ru.finger_use_it_over_711_chords_non_resolv: Use it over 7♯11 chords, non-resolving dominants, jazz and fusion.
ru.finger_the_fifth_mode_of_melodic_minor_i: The fifth mode of melodic minor. It is Mixolydian with a ♭6, producing a darker dominant sound with a minor inflection.
ru.finger_use_it_over_7_13_dominants_resolv: Use it over 7(♭13), dominants resolving to minor and cinematic dominant harmony.
ru.finger_the_sixth_mode_of_melodic_minor_c: The sixth mode of melodic minor. Compared with ordinary Locrian, its natural 2nd softens the tension next to the tonic.
ru.finger_use_it_over_m75_when_a_natural_9_: Use it over m7♭5 when a natural 9 fits the harmony, especially in minor jazz ii–V–i progressions.
ru.finger_the_seventh_mode_of_melodic_minor: The seventh mode of melodic minor. Beyond 1, 3 and ♭7, it contains the altered dominant tensions ♭9, ♯9, ♭5/♯11 and ♭13.
ru.finger_use_it_over_7alt_79_79_75_or_713_: Use it over 7alt, 7♭9, 7♯9, 7♭5 or 7♭13 when a dominant chord requires strong resolution.
ru.finger_the_second_mode_of_harmonic_minor: The second mode of harmonic minor. It keeps Locrian's ♭2 and ♭5 while raising ♭6 to a natural 6th.
ru.finger_use_it_over_m75_when_a_natural_13: Use it over m7♭5 when a natural 13 fits, or for a brighter half-diminished colour than ordinary Locrian.
ru.finger_the_third_mode_of_harmonic_minor_: The third mode of harmonic minor. It is Ionian with a ♯5, creating a maj7♯5 tonic while retaining a natural 4th.
ru.finger_use_it_over_maj75_and_augmented_m: Use it over maj7♯5 and augmented-major harmony when the natural 4th is preferred to Lydian augmented's ♯4.
ru.finger_the_fourth_mode_of_harmonic_minor: The fourth mode of harmonic minor. It keeps Dorian's natural 6th while replacing the natural 4th with ♯4.
ru.finger_use_it_over_m711_fusion_metal_and: Use it over m7♯11, fusion, metal and minor vamps requiring a brighter yet tenser colour than ordinary Dorian.
ru.finger_the_fifth_mode_of_harmonic_minor_: The fifth mode of harmonic minor. Its ♭2 combined with a major 3rd creates a distinctive dominant sound unlike ordinary Phrygian.
ru.finger_use_it_over_v7_in_minor_keys_9_13: Use it over V7 in minor keys, ♭9/♭13 dominants, metal, fusion and many flamenco contexts.
ru.finger_the_sixth_mode_of_harmonic_minor_: The sixth mode of harmonic minor. It combines ♯2 with Lydian's ♯4, creating an augmented second near the tonic.
ru.finger_use_it_over_maj711_when_a_9_2_fit: Use it over maj7♯11 when a ♯9/♯2 fits the line, mainly in advanced composition and jazz contexts.
ru.finger_the_seventh_mode_of_harmonic_mino: The seventh mode of harmonic minor. It is highly tense, with ♭4, ♭5 and a doubly lowered 7th; it is not the melodic-minor Altered/Super Locrian scale.
ru.finger_use_sparingly_in_composition_dimi: Use sparingly in composition, diminished/altered harmony and advanced ear training; always read it together with its formula.
ru.finger_a_six_note_scale_built_entirely_f: A six-note scale built entirely from whole steps. With no semitones, it sounds floating and unresolved.
ru.finger_use_it_over_augmented_harmony_and: Use it over augmented harmony and dominant chords with ♯5/♭5 for an ambiguous, symmetrical colour.
ru.finger_an_eight_note_symmetrical_scale_a: An eight-note symmetrical scale alternating half and whole steps. It contains a dominant chord plus several altered tensions.
ru.finger_use_it_over_79_79_139_and_dominan: Use it over 7♭9, 7♯9, 13♭9 and dominant-diminished harmony, especially before resolution.
ru.finger_an_eight_note_symmetrical_scale_a: An eight-note symmetrical scale alternating whole and half steps. It outlines a diminished-seventh chord from the tonic.
ru.finger_use_it_over_7_harmony_diminished_: Use it over °7 harmony, diminished sequences and minor-third transposition practice.
ru.finger_the_chromatic_scale_contains_all_: The chromatic scale contains all 12 pitch classes in the octave. It is not a major-scale mode but the complete semitone collection.
ru.finger_use_it_for_technique_chromatic_ap: Use it for technique, chromatic approaches between chord tones, semitone ear training and chromatic line development.
ru.finger_mixolydian_plus_a_major_7th_passi: Mixolydian plus a major 7th passing tone. With suitable rhythmic placement, chord tones can align consistently with strong beats.
ru.finger_use_it_over_dominant_seventh_harm: Use it over dominant-seventh harmony in bebop and jazz; practise it rhythmically rather than only as a mechanical up-and-down scale.
ru.finger_a_major_scale_with_a_lowered_6th_: A major scale with a lowered 6th, combining a major tonic with the ♭6 colour often associated with minor harmony.
ru.finger_use_it_over_maj7_13_borrowed_harm: Use it over maj7(♭13), borrowed harmony and major-key lines requiring a darker colour.
ru.finger_a_major_scale_with_2_and_6_creati: A major scale with ♭2 and ♭6, creating two characteristic augmented seconds. Some Western sources also call it Byzantine.
ru.finger_use_it_for_western_labelled_middl: Use it for Western-labelled Middle Eastern/Mediterranean colours, metal, fusion and composition requiring strong tension.
ru.finger_ritusen_yo_pentatonic_mode_12456_: Ritusen/Yo pentatonic mode: 1–2–4–5–6. With G as tonic, G–A–C–D–E shares the pitches of C major pentatonic, so its open C-reference shape is valid while G stays the root (R). This differs from dominant 1–3–4–5–b7.
ru.finger_use_for_open_suspended_pentatonic: Use for open/suspended pentatonic sounds. In G, the C-major reference shape occupies open strings through fret 4; keep G as the tonal centre.
ru.finger_tuner_tools_uses_the_common_weste: Tuner Tools uses the common Western reference form 1–2–♭3–5–♭6. Naming and pitches can vary with tuning, instrument and Japanese tradition.
ru.finger_useful_for_pentatonic_melody_writ: Useful for pentatonic melody writing with wide gaps, a dark colour and interval-control practice.
ru.finger_the_western_reference_form_12457_: The Western reference form 1–♭2–4–5–♭7 creates a dark suspended colour. Traditional terminology can vary by source and tuning.
ru.finger_useful_over_sus_harmony_dark_melo: Useful over sus harmony, dark melody, ambient, metal and exercises emphasizing the ♭2.
ru.finger_the_western_reference_form_12457_: The Western reference form 1–♭2–4–♭5–♭7 has strongly tense ♭2 and ♭5 degrees. Its historical name should not be treated as one absolutely fixed Western mode.
ru.finger_useful_for_dark_melody_sound_desi: Useful for dark melody, sound design, metal and ear training with tense intervals.
ru.finger_a_custom_roman_numeral_loop_that_: A custom Roman-numeral loop that is saved automatically and transposes to every key.
ru.finger_the_dominant_of_the_target_chord_: The dominant of the target chord; its 3rd and 7th pull clearly into {0}.
ru.finger_the_diminished_chord_root_lies_a_: The diminished chord root lies a semitone below {0}, resolving upward into the destination root.
ru.finger_a_dominant_a_semitone_above_the_t: A dominant a semitone above the target, useful in jazz with a strong chromatic bass line.
ru.finger_keep_the_hand_relaxed_and_play_1_: Keep the hand relaxed and play 1-2-3-4 evenly across six strings.
ru.finger_each_finger_owns_one_fret_alterna: Each finger owns one fret; alternate picking synchronizes both hands.
ru.finger_apply_the_same_pulse_to_a_short_c: Apply the same pulse to a short chromatic line.
ru.finger_change_strings_without_breaking_t: Change strings without breaking the pulse and keep the picking motion compact.
ru.finger_alternate_picking_continues_throu: Alternate picking continues through string changes instead of restarting on each string.
ru.finger_use_this_motion_in_riffs_and_mult: Use this motion in riffs and multi-string solo lines.
ru.finger_separate_each_finger_movement_esp: Separate each finger movement, especially fingers 3 and 4.
ru.finger_lift_only_the_moving_finger_and_k: Lift only the moving finger and keep the others close to the strings.
ru.finger_prepare_for_scale_and_arpeggio_li: Prepare for scale and arpeggio lines with changing finger order.
ru.finger_keep_planted_fingers_down_while_t: Keep planted fingers down while the next finger crosses to the adjacent string.
