ja.finger_seventh_chords_through_the_circle: 4度サークルのセブンスコード
ja.finger_lesson_13_has_3_parts_13a_major_1: Lesson 13 has 3 parts: 13A Major → 13B Em7/E7 → 13C Minor
ja.finger_roots_on_strings_5_and_2_the_c_ma: Roots on strings 5 and 2; the C-major reference box spans frets 0-3
ja.finger_roots_on_strings_5_and_3_the_c_ma: Roots on strings 5 and 3; the C-major reference box spans frets 2-6
ja.finger_roots_on_strings_6_3_and_1_the_c_: Roots on strings 6, 3 and 1; the C-major reference box spans frets 5-8
ja.finger_roots_on_strings_6_4_and_1_the_c_: Roots on strings 6, 4 and 1; the C-major reference box spans frets 7-10
ja.finger_roots_on_strings_4_and_2_the_c_ma: Roots on strings 4 and 2; the C-major reference box spans frets 9-13
ja.finger_ionian_is_the_standard_major_scal: Ionian is the standard major scale. Its major 7th creates a strong pull toward the tonic.
ja.finger_use_it_over_major_and_maj7_harmon: Use it over major and maj7 harmony and conventional major-key melodies.
ja.finger_dorian_is_a_minor_mode_with_a_nat: Dorian is a minor mode with a natural 6th, giving it a brighter sound than Aeolian.
ja.finger_useful_over_m7_and_m6_harmony_fun: Useful over m7 and m6 harmony, funk, jazz and Dorian vamps.
ja.finger_phrygian_is_a_minor_mode_whose_ch: Phrygian is a minor mode whose characteristic ♭2 creates a dark, tense pull near the tonic.
ja.finger_useful_over_static_minor_harmony_: Useful over static minor harmony, metal and Spanish-flavoured lines; it is not the same as Phrygian dominant.
ja.finger_lydian_is_a_major_mode_with_a_cha: Lydian is a major mode with a characteristic ♯4, producing a bright and open sound.
ja.finger_useful_over_maj7_and_maj711_harmo: Useful over maj7 and maj7♯11 harmony and modern, floating major sounds.
ja.finger_mixolydian_is_a_major_mode_with_a: Mixolydian is a major mode with a ♭7. The major 3rd and ♭7 clearly outline dominant function.
ja.finger_use_it_over_dominant_seventh_harm: Use it over dominant-seventh harmony, blues, rock, funk and Mixolydian progressions.
ja.finger_aeolian_is_the_natural_minor_scal: Aeolian is the natural minor scale. Its ♭6 is an important contrast with Dorian.
ja.finger_use_it_over_minor_harmony_natural: Use it over minor harmony, natural-minor progressions and stable, darker melodies.
ja.finger_locrian_is_a_minor_mode_with_a_5_: Locrian is a minor mode with a ♭5 and ♭2, so its tonic harmony is inherently unstable.
ja.finger_useful_over_m75_half_diminished_h: Useful over m7♭5 (half-diminished) harmony, ear training and highly tense passages.
ja.finger_harmonic_minor_3840b788: ハーモニックマイナー
ja.finger_harmonic_minor_raises_the_7th_of_: Harmonic minor raises the 7th of natural minor. The ♭6–7 span creates a strong pull to the tonic and its characteristic harmonic colour.
ja.finger_use_it_in_minor_key_harmony_espec: Use it in minor-key harmony, especially V7 resolving to i, as well as classical metal, neoclassical and many flamenco contexts.
ja.finger_melodic_minor_jazz_bcc31317: メロディックマイナー（ジャズ）
ja.finger_this_is_the_jazz_melodic_minor_fo: This is the jazz melodic-minor form: the same collection ascending and descending. It can be heard as a major scale with a lowered 3rd.
ja.finger_use_it_over_m_maj7_and_m6_harmony: Use it over m(maj7) and m6 harmony and as the parent scale of Lydian dominant, Altered and the other melodic-minor modes.
ja.finger_major_pentatonic_efb6f712: メジャー・ペンタトニック
ja.finger_a_bright_accessible_pentatonic_sc: A bright, accessible pentatonic scale with few avoid notes.
ja.finger_useful_for_pop_country_and_soloin: Useful for pop, country and soloing over major chords.
ja.finger_minor_pentatonic_201f7ebd: マイナー・ペンタトニック
ja.finger_the_familiar_minor_pentatonic_sou: The familiar minor pentatonic sound used in blues and rock.
ja.finger_useful_for_blues_rock_and_soloing: Useful for blues, rock and soloing over minor chords.
ja.finger_a_variant_formed_by_omitting_degr: A variant formed by omitting degrees 2 and 6 from Mixolydian. “With 4” is shown because methods do not use one universal naming convention.
ja.finger_keeps_the_major_3rd_and_7_and_add: Keeps the major 3rd and ♭7 and adds the 4th; useful over dominant 7, 7sus4, funk and rock.
ja.finger_a_dominant_seventh_outline_plus_d: A dominant-seventh outline plus degree 2/9. Some methods also call it Mixolydian pentatonic.
ja.finger_useful_over_dominant_7_9_harmony_: Useful over dominant 7/9 harmony in jazz, blues and funk, especially when avoiding the 4th.
ja.finger_the_major_blues_scale_is_major_pe: The major blues scale is major pentatonic plus ♭3. The expressive tension between ♭3 and 3 creates its blues colour.
ja.finger_useful_for_major_blues_country_an: Useful for major blues, country and rock and roll over major or dominant harmony, treating ♭3 as a blue note.
ja.finger_the_minor_blues_scale_is_minor_pe: The minor blues scale is minor pentatonic plus ♭5. The ♭5 is its characteristic blue note, often approached or bent toward 5.
ja.finger_useful_for_blues_and_rock_over_mi: Useful for blues and rock over minor or dominant harmony, depending on the harmonic context.
ja.finger_the_second_mode_of_melodic_minor_: The second mode of melodic minor. It keeps Dorian's natural 6th while adding a dark, tense ♭2.
ja.finger_useful_over_m7_9_minor_sus_harmon: Useful over m7(♭9), minor-sus harmony and jazz/fusion passages requiring a darker Dorian colour.
ja.finger_the_third_mode_of_melodic_minor_c: The third mode of melodic minor, combining Lydian's ♯4 with the augmented chord's ♯5.
ja.finger_use_it_over_maj75_maj7115_and_mod: Use it over maj7♯5, maj7♯11♯5 and modern augmented-major harmony.
ja.finger_the_fourth_mode_of_melodic_minor_: The fourth mode of melodic minor, also called Lydian ♭7. It combines ♯4/♯11 with the dominant major 3rd and ♭7.
ja.finger_use_it_over_711_chords_non_resolv: Use it over 7♯11 chords, non-resolving dominants, jazz and fusion.
ja.finger_the_fifth_mode_of_melodic_minor_i: The fifth mode of melodic minor. It is Mixolydian with a ♭6, producing a darker dominant sound with a minor inflection.
ja.finger_use_it_over_7_13_dominants_resolv: Use it over 7(♭13), dominants resolving to minor and cinematic dominant harmony.
ja.finger_the_sixth_mode_of_melodic_minor_c: The sixth mode of melodic minor. Compared with ordinary Locrian, its natural 2nd softens the tension next to the tonic.
ja.finger_use_it_over_m75_when_a_natural_9_: Use it over m7♭5 when a natural 9 fits the harmony, especially in minor jazz ii–V–i progressions.
ja.finger_the_seventh_mode_of_melodic_minor: The seventh mode of melodic minor. Beyond 1, 3 and ♭7, it contains the altered dominant tensions ♭9, ♯9, ♭5/♯11 and ♭13.
ja.finger_use_it_over_7alt_79_79_75_or_713_: Use it over 7alt, 7♭9, 7♯9, 7♭5 or 7♭13 when a dominant chord requires strong resolution.
ja.finger_the_second_mode_of_harmonic_minor: The second mode of harmonic minor. It keeps Locrian's ♭2 and ♭5 while raising ♭6 to a natural 6th.
ja.finger_use_it_over_m75_when_a_natural_13: Use it over m7♭5 when a natural 13 fits, or for a brighter half-diminished colour than ordinary Locrian.
ja.finger_the_third_mode_of_harmonic_minor_: The third mode of harmonic minor. It is Ionian with a ♯5, creating a maj7♯5 tonic while retaining a natural 4th.
ja.finger_use_it_over_maj75_and_augmented_m: Use it over maj7♯5 and augmented-major harmony when the natural 4th is preferred to Lydian augmented's ♯4.
ja.finger_the_fourth_mode_of_harmonic_minor: The fourth mode of harmonic minor. It keeps Dorian's natural 6th while replacing the natural 4th with ♯4.
ja.finger_use_it_over_m711_fusion_metal_and: Use it over m7♯11, fusion, metal and minor vamps requiring a brighter yet tenser colour than ordinary Dorian.
ja.finger_the_fifth_mode_of_harmonic_minor_: The fifth mode of harmonic minor. Its ♭2 combined with a major 3rd creates a distinctive dominant sound unlike ordinary Phrygian.
ja.finger_use_it_over_v7_in_minor_keys_9_13: Use it over V7 in minor keys, ♭9/♭13 dominants, metal, fusion and many flamenco contexts.
ja.finger_the_sixth_mode_of_harmonic_minor_: The sixth mode of harmonic minor. It combines ♯2 with Lydian's ♯4, creating an augmented second near the tonic.
ja.finger_use_it_over_maj711_when_a_9_2_fit: Use it over maj7♯11 when a ♯9/♯2 fits the line, mainly in advanced composition and jazz contexts.
ja.finger_the_seventh_mode_of_harmonic_mino: The seventh mode of harmonic minor. It is highly tense, with ♭4, ♭5 and a doubly lowered 7th; it is not the melodic-minor Altered/Super Locrian scale.
ja.finger_use_sparingly_in_composition_dimi: Use sparingly in composition, diminished/altered harmony and advanced ear training; always read it together with its formula.
ja.finger_a_six_note_scale_built_entirely_f: A six-note scale built entirely from whole steps. With no semitones, it sounds floating and unresolved.
ja.finger_use_it_over_augmented_harmony_and: Use it over augmented harmony and dominant chords with ♯5/♭5 for an ambiguous, symmetrical colour.
ja.finger_an_eight_note_symmetrical_scale_a: An eight-note symmetrical scale alternating half and whole steps. It contains a dominant chord plus several altered tensions.
ja.finger_use_it_over_79_79_139_and_dominan: Use it over 7♭9, 7♯9, 13♭9 and dominant-diminished harmony, especially before resolution.
ja.finger_an_eight_note_symmetrical_scale_a: An eight-note symmetrical scale alternating whole and half steps. It outlines a diminished-seventh chord from the tonic.
ja.finger_use_it_over_7_harmony_diminished_: Use it over °7 harmony, diminished sequences and minor-third transposition practice.
ja.finger_the_chromatic_scale_contains_all_: The chromatic scale contains all 12 pitch classes in the octave. It is not a major-scale mode but the complete semitone collection.
ja.finger_use_it_for_technique_chromatic_ap: Use it for technique, chromatic approaches between chord tones, semitone ear training and chromatic line development.
ja.finger_mixolydian_plus_a_major_7th_passi: Mixolydian plus a major 7th passing tone. With suitable rhythmic placement, chord tones can align consistently with strong beats.
ja.finger_use_it_over_dominant_seventh_harm: Use it over dominant-seventh harmony in bebop and jazz; practise it rhythmically rather than only as a mechanical up-and-down scale.
ja.finger_a_major_scale_with_a_lowered_6th_: A major scale with a lowered 6th, combining a major tonic with the ♭6 colour often associated with minor harmony.
ja.finger_use_it_over_maj7_13_borrowed_harm: Use it over maj7(♭13), borrowed harmony and major-key lines requiring a darker colour.
ja.finger_a_major_scale_with_2_and_6_creati: A major scale with ♭2 and ♭6, creating two characteristic augmented seconds. Some Western sources also call it Byzantine.
ja.finger_use_it_for_western_labelled_middl: Use it for Western-labelled Middle Eastern/Mediterranean colours, metal, fusion and composition requiring strong tension.
ja.finger_ritusen_yo_pentatonic_mode_12456_: Ritusen/Yo pentatonic mode: 1–2–4–5–6. With G as tonic, G–A–C–D–E shares the pitches of C major pentatonic, so its open C-reference shape is valid while G stays the root (R). This differs from dominant 1–3–4–5–b7.
ja.finger_use_for_open_suspended_pentatonic: Use for open/suspended pentatonic sounds. In G, the C-major reference shape occupies open strings through fret 4; keep G as the tonal centre.
ja.finger_tuner_tools_uses_the_common_weste: Tuner Tools uses the common Western reference form 1–2–♭3–5–♭6. Naming and pitches can vary with tuning, instrument and Japanese tradition.
ja.finger_useful_for_pentatonic_melody_writ: Useful for pentatonic melody writing with wide gaps, a dark colour and interval-control practice.
ja.finger_the_western_reference_form_12457_: The Western reference form 1–♭2–4–5–♭7 creates a dark suspended colour. Traditional terminology can vary by source and tuning.
ja.finger_useful_over_sus_harmony_dark_melo: Useful over sus harmony, dark melody, ambient, metal and exercises emphasizing the ♭2.
ja.finger_the_western_reference_form_12457_: The Western reference form 1–♭2–4–♭5–♭7 has strongly tense ♭2 and ♭5 degrees. Its historical name should not be treated as one absolutely fixed Western mode.
ja.finger_useful_for_dark_melody_sound_desi: Useful for dark melody, sound design, metal and ear training with tense intervals.
ja.finger_a_custom_roman_numeral_loop_that_: A custom Roman-numeral loop that is saved automatically and transposes to every key.
ja.finger_the_dominant_of_the_target_chord_: The dominant of the target chord; its 3rd and 7th pull clearly into {0}.
ja.finger_the_diminished_chord_root_lies_a_: The diminished chord root lies a semitone below {0}, resolving upward into the destination root.
ja.finger_a_dominant_a_semitone_above_the_t: A dominant a semitone above the target, useful in jazz with a strong chromatic bass line.
ja.finger_keep_the_hand_relaxed_and_play_1_: Keep the hand relaxed and play 1-2-3-4 evenly across six strings.
ja.finger_each_finger_owns_one_fret_alterna: Each finger owns one fret; alternate picking synchronizes both hands.
ja.finger_apply_the_same_pulse_to_a_short_c: Apply the same pulse to a short chromatic line.
ja.finger_change_strings_without_breaking_t: Change strings without breaking the pulse and keep the picking motion compact.
ja.finger_alternate_picking_continues_throu: Alternate picking continues through string changes instead of restarting on each string.
ja.finger_use_this_motion_in_riffs_and_mult: Use this motion in riffs and multi-string solo lines.
ja.finger_separate_each_finger_movement_esp: Separate each finger movement, especially fingers 3 and 4.
ja.finger_lift_only_the_moving_finger_and_k: Lift only the moving finger and keep the others close to the strings.
ja.finger_prepare_for_scale_and_arpeggio_li: Prepare for scale and arpeggio lines with changing finger order.
ja.finger_keep_planted_fingers_down_while_t: Keep planted fingers down while the next finger crosses to the adjacent string.
ja.finger_the_spider_drill_develops_finger_: The Spider drill develops finger independence and two-hand string control.
ja.finger_useful_for_chords_legato_and_diag: Useful for chords, legato and diagonal string-crossing lines.
ja.finger_keep_an_even_pulse_between_1_2_3_: Keep an even pulse between 1-2-3 and 2-3-4 groups.
ja.finger_sequences_create_musical_phrasing: Sequences create musical phrasing instead of merely running straight up and down.
ja.finger_use_three_note_groups_to_build_sc: Use three-note groups to build scale-based solo phrases.
ja.finger_hammer_on_pull_off_1ec8e42e: ハンマリングとプリング
ja.finger_produce_even_notes_with_the_frett: Produce even notes with the fretting hand without repicking every note.
ja.finger_pick_the_first_note_then_articula: Pick the first note, then articulate with the fretting hand while staying in time.
ja.finger_apply_it_to_legato_phrases_and_po: Apply it to legato phrases and position connections.
ja.finger_hear_and_see_the_root_third_and_f: Hear and see the root, third and fifth through an I-IV-V progression.
ja.finger_the_third_defines_major_or_minor_: The third defines major or minor quality; the fifth adds stability.
ja.finger_play_c_f_g_on_strings_1_2_3_with_: Play C-F-G on strings 1-2-3 with an even pulse.
ja.finger_triads_three_inversions_c03c2ad1: トライアド・3つの転回形
ja.finger_recognize_root_position_first_and: Recognize root position, first and second inversion in one fretboard area.
ja.finger_the_lowest_note_determines_the_in: The lowest note determines the inversion while the three chord tones remain the same.
ja.finger_connect_i_iv_v_with_the_nearest_i: Connect I-IV-V with the nearest inversion instead of large position jumps.
ja.finger_triads_seven_chords_in_a_major_ke: トライアド・長調の7コード
ja.finger_play_i_ii_iii_iv_v_vi_vii_and_rec: Play I-ii-iii-IV-V-vi-vii° and recognize root, first and second inversion on strings 1-2-3.
ja.finger_in_every_major_key_the_seven_tria: In every major key, the seven triads follow: Major-Minor-Minor-Major-Major-Minor-Diminished.
ja.finger_in_c_c_dm_em_f_g_am_bdim_this_map: In C: C-Dm-Em-F-G-Am-Bdim; this map supports accompaniment, analysis and progression building.
ja.finger_connect_dm_g_c_with_minimal_hand_: Connect Dm-G-C with minimal hand movement.
ja.finger_ii_prepares_v_creates_tension_and: ii prepares, V creates tension and I provides resolution.
ja.finger_use_it_in_ballads_jazz_and_chord_: Use it in ballads, jazz and chord-tone soloing.
ja.finger_triads_pop_voice_leading_59124e78: トライアド・ポップの声部進行
ja.finger_connect_i_v_vi_iv_using_common_to: Connect I-V-vi-IV using common tones and nearest inversions.
ja.finger_retaining_common_tones_smooths_ch: Retaining common tones smooths chord changes and reduces unnecessary motion.
ja.finger_apply_it_directly_to_modern_pop_a: Apply it directly to modern pop and ballad accompaniment.
ja.finger_seventh_chords_arpeggios_guide_to: セブンスコード・アルペジオとガイドトーン
ja.finger_play_dm7_g7_cmaj7_and_hear_the_co: Play Dm7-G7-Cmaj7 and hear the color of each seventh.
ja.finger_the_third_and_seventh_are_guide_t: The third and seventh are guide tones that reveal harmonic function.
ja.finger_resolve_phrases_to_the_third_or_s: Resolve phrases to the third or seventh over a ii-V-I.
ja.finger_run_cmaj7_fmaj7_bm75_em7_am7_dm7_: Run Cmaj7-Fmaj7-Bm7♭5-Em7-Am7-Dm7-G7 and hear G7 resolve to Cmaj7.

zh.finger_ionian_is_the_standard_major_scal: Ionian is the standard major scale. Its major 7th creates a strong pull toward the tonic.
zh.finger_use_it_over_major_and_maj7_harmon: Use it over major and maj7 harmony and conventional major-key melodies.
zh.finger_dorian_is_a_minor_mode_with_a_nat: Dorian is a minor mode with a natural 6th, giving it a brighter sound than Aeolian.
zh.finger_useful_over_m7_and_m6_harmony_fun: Useful over m7 and m6 harmony, funk, jazz and Dorian vamps.
zh.finger_phrygian_is_a_minor_mode_whose_ch: Phrygian is a minor mode whose characteristic ♭2 creates a dark, tense pull near the tonic.
zh.finger_useful_over_static_minor_harmony_: Useful over static minor harmony, metal and Spanish-flavoured lines; it is not the same as Phrygian dominant.
zh.finger_lydian_is_a_major_mode_with_a_cha: Lydian is a major mode with a characteristic ♯4, producing a bright and open sound.
zh.finger_useful_over_maj7_and_maj711_harmo: Useful over maj7 and maj7♯11 harmony and modern, floating major sounds.
zh.finger_mixolydian_is_a_major_mode_with_a: Mixolydian is a major mode with a ♭7. The major 3rd and ♭7 clearly outline dominant function.
zh.finger_use_it_over_dominant_seventh_harm: Use it over dominant-seventh harmony, blues, rock, funk and Mixolydian progressions.
zh.finger_aeolian_is_the_natural_minor_scal: Aeolian is the natural minor scale. Its ♭6 is an important contrast with Dorian.
zh.finger_use_it_over_minor_harmony_natural: Use it over minor harmony, natural-minor progressions and stable, darker melodies.
zh.finger_locrian_is_a_minor_mode_with_a_5_: Locrian is a minor mode with a ♭5 and ♭2, so its tonic harmony is inherently unstable.
zh.finger_useful_over_m75_half_diminished_h: Useful over m7♭5 (half-diminished) harmony, ear training and highly tense passages.
zh.finger_harmonic_minor_raises_the_7th_of_: Harmonic minor raises the 7th of natural minor. The ♭6–7 span creates a strong pull to the tonic and its characteristic harmonic colour.
zh.finger_use_it_in_minor_key_harmony_espec: Use it in minor-key harmony, especially V7 resolving to i, as well as classical metal, neoclassical and many flamenco contexts.
zh.finger_this_is_the_jazz_melodic_minor_fo: This is the jazz melodic-minor form: the same collection ascending and descending. It can be heard as a major scale with a lowered 3rd.
zh.finger_use_it_over_m_maj7_and_m6_harmony: Use it over m(maj7) and m6 harmony and as the parent scale of Lydian dominant, Altered and the other melodic-minor modes.
zh.finger_a_bright_accessible_pentatonic_sc: A bright, accessible pentatonic scale with few avoid notes.
zh.finger_useful_for_pop_country_and_soloin: Useful for pop, country and soloing over major chords.
zh.finger_the_familiar_minor_pentatonic_sou: The familiar minor pentatonic sound used in blues and rock.
zh.finger_useful_for_blues_rock_and_soloing: Useful for blues, rock and soloing over minor chords.
zh.finger_a_variant_formed_by_omitting_degr: A variant formed by omitting degrees 2 and 6 from Mixolydian. “With 4” is shown because methods do not use one universal naming convention.
zh.finger_keeps_the_major_3rd_and_7_and_add: Keeps the major 3rd and ♭7 and adds the 4th; useful over dominant 7, 7sus4, funk and rock.
zh.finger_a_dominant_seventh_outline_plus_d: A dominant-seventh outline plus degree 2/9. Some methods also call it Mixolydian pentatonic.
zh.finger_useful_over_dominant_7_9_harmony_: Useful over dominant 7/9 harmony in jazz, blues and funk, especially when avoiding the 4th.
zh.finger_the_major_blues_scale_is_major_pe: The major blues scale is major pentatonic plus ♭3. The expressive tension between ♭3 and 3 creates its blues colour.
zh.finger_useful_for_major_blues_country_an: Useful for major blues, country and rock and roll over major or dominant harmony, treating ♭3 as a blue note.
zh.finger_the_minor_blues_scale_is_minor_pe: The minor blues scale is minor pentatonic plus ♭5. The ♭5 is its characteristic blue note, often approached or bent toward 5.
zh.finger_useful_for_blues_and_rock_over_mi: Useful for blues and rock over minor or dominant harmony, depending on the harmonic context.
zh.finger_the_second_mode_of_melodic_minor_: The second mode of melodic minor. It keeps Dorian's natural 6th while adding a dark, tense ♭2.
zh.finger_useful_over_m7_9_minor_sus_harmon: Useful over m7(♭9), minor-sus harmony and jazz/fusion passages requiring a darker Dorian colour.
zh.finger_the_third_mode_of_melodic_minor_c: The third mode of melodic minor, combining Lydian's ♯4 with the augmented chord's ♯5.
zh.finger_use_it_over_maj75_maj7115_and_mod: Use it over maj7♯5, maj7♯11♯5 and modern augmented-major harmony.
zh.finger_the_fourth_mode_of_melodic_minor_: The fourth mode of melodic minor, also called Lydian ♭7. It combines ♯4/♯11 with the dominant major 3rd and ♭7.
zh.finger_use_it_over_711_chords_non_resolv: Use it over 7♯11 chords, non-resolving dominants, jazz and fusion.
zh.finger_the_fifth_mode_of_melodic_minor_i: The fifth mode of melodic minor. It is Mixolydian with a ♭6, producing a darker dominant sound with a minor inflection.
zh.finger_use_it_over_7_13_dominants_resolv: Use it over 7(♭13), dominants resolving to minor and cinematic dominant harmony.
zh.finger_the_sixth_mode_of_melodic_minor_c: The sixth mode of melodic minor. Compared with ordinary Locrian, its natural 2nd softens the tension next to the tonic.
zh.finger_use_it_over_m75_when_a_natural_9_: Use it over m7♭5 when a natural 9 fits the harmony, especially in minor jazz ii–V–i progressions.
zh.finger_the_seventh_mode_of_melodic_minor: The seventh mode of melodic minor. Beyond 1, 3 and ♭7, it contains the altered dominant tensions ♭9, ♯9, ♭5/♯11 and ♭13.
zh.finger_use_it_over_7alt_79_79_75_or_713_: Use it over 7alt, 7♭9, 7♯9, 7♭5 or 7♭13 when a dominant chord requires strong resolution.
zh.finger_the_second_mode_of_harmonic_minor: The second mode of harmonic minor. It keeps Locrian's ♭2 and ♭5 while raising ♭6 to a natural 6th.
zh.finger_use_it_over_m75_when_a_natural_13: Use it over m7♭5 when a natural 13 fits, or for a brighter half-diminished colour than ordinary Locrian.
zh.finger_the_third_mode_of_harmonic_minor_: The third mode of harmonic minor. It is Ionian with a ♯5, creating a maj7♯5 tonic while retaining a natural 4th.
zh.finger_use_it_over_maj75_and_augmented_m: Use it over maj7♯5 and augmented-major harmony when the natural 4th is preferred to Lydian augmented's ♯4.
zh.finger_the_fourth_mode_of_harmonic_minor: The fourth mode of harmonic minor. It keeps Dorian's natural 6th while replacing the natural 4th with ♯4.
zh.finger_use_it_over_m711_fusion_metal_and: Use it over m7♯11, fusion, metal and minor vamps requiring a brighter yet tenser colour than ordinary Dorian.
zh.finger_the_fifth_mode_of_harmonic_minor_: The fifth mode of harmonic minor. Its ♭2 combined with a major 3rd creates a distinctive dominant sound unlike ordinary Phrygian.
zh.finger_use_it_over_v7_in_minor_keys_9_13: Use it over V7 in minor keys, ♭9/♭13 dominants, metal, fusion and many flamenco contexts.
zh.finger_the_sixth_mode_of_harmonic_minor_: The sixth mode of harmonic minor. It combines ♯2 with Lydian's ♯4, creating an augmented second near the tonic.
zh.finger_use_it_over_maj711_when_a_9_2_fit: Use it over maj7♯11 when a ♯9/♯2 fits the line, mainly in advanced composition and jazz contexts.
zh.finger_the_seventh_mode_of_harmonic_mino: The seventh mode of harmonic minor. It is highly tense, with ♭4, ♭5 and a doubly lowered 7th; it is not the melodic-minor Altered/Super Locrian scale.
zh.finger_use_sparingly_in_composition_dimi: Use sparingly in composition, diminished/altered harmony and advanced ear training; always read it together with its formula.
zh.finger_a_six_note_scale_built_entirely_f: A six-note scale built entirely from whole steps. With no semitones, it sounds floating and unresolved.
zh.finger_use_it_over_augmented_harmony_and: Use it over augmented harmony and dominant chords with ♯5/♭5 for an ambiguous, symmetrical colour.
zh.finger_an_eight_note_symmetrical_scale_a: An eight-note symmetrical scale alternating half and whole steps. It contains a dominant chord plus several altered tensions.
zh.finger_use_it_over_79_79_139_and_dominan: Use it over 7♭9, 7♯9, 13♭9 and dominant-diminished harmony, especially before resolution.
zh.finger_an_eight_note_symmetrical_scale_a: An eight-note symmetrical scale alternating whole and half steps. It outlines a diminished-seventh chord from the tonic.
zh.finger_use_it_over_7_harmony_diminished_: Use it over °7 harmony, diminished sequences and minor-third transposition practice.
zh.finger_the_chromatic_scale_contains_all_: The chromatic scale contains all 12 pitch classes in the octave. It is not a major-scale mode but the complete semitone collection.
zh.finger_use_it_for_technique_chromatic_ap: Use it for technique, chromatic approaches between chord tones, semitone ear training and chromatic line development.
zh.finger_mixolydian_plus_a_major_7th_passi: Mixolydian plus a major 7th passing tone. With suitable rhythmic placement, chord tones can align consistently with strong beats.
zh.finger_use_it_over_dominant_seventh_harm: Use it over dominant-seventh harmony in bebop and jazz; practise it rhythmically rather than only as a mechanical up-and-down scale.
zh.finger_a_major_scale_with_a_lowered_6th_: A major scale with a lowered 6th, combining a major tonic with the ♭6 colour often associated with minor harmony.
zh.finger_use_it_over_maj7_13_borrowed_harm: Use it over maj7(♭13), borrowed harmony and major-key lines requiring a darker colour.
zh.finger_a_major_scale_with_2_and_6_creati: A major scale with ♭2 and ♭6, creating two characteristic augmented seconds. Some Western sources also call it Byzantine.
zh.finger_use_it_for_western_labelled_middl: Use it for Western-labelled Middle Eastern/Mediterranean colours, metal, fusion and composition requiring strong tension.
zh.finger_ritusen_yo_pentatonic_mode_12456_: Ritusen/Yo pentatonic mode: 1–2–4–5–6. With G as tonic, G–A–C–D–E shares the pitches of C major pentatonic, so its open C-reference shape is valid while G stays the root (R). This differs from dominant 1–3–4–5–b7.
zh.finger_use_for_open_suspended_pentatonic: Use for open/suspended pentatonic sounds. In G, the C-major reference shape occupies open strings through fret 4; keep G as the tonal centre.
zh.finger_tuner_tools_uses_the_common_weste: Tuner Tools uses the common Western reference form 1–2–♭3–5–♭6. Naming and pitches can vary with tuning, instrument and Japanese tradition.
zh.finger_useful_for_pentatonic_melody_writ: Useful for pentatonic melody writing with wide gaps, a dark colour and interval-control practice.
zh.finger_the_western_reference_form_12457_: The Western reference form 1–♭2–4–5–♭7 creates a dark suspended colour. Traditional terminology can vary by source and tuning.
zh.finger_useful_over_sus_harmony_dark_melo: Useful over sus harmony, dark melody, ambient, metal and exercises emphasizing the ♭2.
zh.finger_the_western_reference_form_12457_: The Western reference form 1–♭2–4–♭5–♭7 has strongly tense ♭2 and ♭5 degrees. Its historical name should not be treated as one absolutely fixed Western mode.
zh.finger_useful_for_dark_melody_sound_desi: Useful for dark melody, sound design, metal and ear training with tense intervals.

lo.finger_seventh_chords_through_the_circle: ຄອດ 7 ໃນວົງຄວອດ
lo.finger_lesson_13_has_3_parts_13a_major_1: Lesson 13 has 3 parts: 13A Major → 13B Em7/E7 → 13C Minor
lo.finger_roots_on_strings_5_and_2_the_c_ma: Roots on strings 5 and 2; the C-major reference box spans frets 0-3
lo.finger_roots_on_strings_5_and_3_the_c_ma: Roots on strings 5 and 3; the C-major reference box spans frets 2-6
lo.finger_roots_on_strings_6_3_and_1_the_c_: Roots on strings 6, 3 and 1; the C-major reference box spans frets 5-8
lo.finger_roots_on_strings_6_4_and_1_the_c_: Roots on strings 6, 4 and 1; the C-major reference box spans frets 7-10
lo.finger_roots_on_strings_4_and_2_the_c_ma: Roots on strings 4 and 2; the C-major reference box spans frets 9-13
lo.finger_ionian_is_the_standard_major_scal: Ionian is the standard major scale. Its major 7th creates a strong pull toward the tonic.
lo.finger_use_it_over_major_and_maj7_harmon: Use it over major and maj7 harmony and conventional major-key melodies.
lo.finger_dorian_is_a_minor_mode_with_a_nat: Dorian is a minor mode with a natural 6th, giving it a brighter sound than Aeolian.
lo.finger_useful_over_m7_and_m6_harmony_fun: Useful over m7 and m6 harmony, funk, jazz and Dorian vamps.
lo.finger_phrygian_is_a_minor_mode_whose_ch: Phrygian is a minor mode whose characteristic ♭2 creates a dark, tense pull near the tonic.
lo.finger_useful_over_static_minor_harmony_: Useful over static minor harmony, metal and Spanish-flavoured lines; it is not the same as Phrygian dominant.
lo.finger_lydian_is_a_major_mode_with_a_cha: Lydian is a major mode with a characteristic ♯4, producing a bright and open sound.
lo.finger_useful_over_maj7_and_maj711_harmo: Useful over maj7 and maj7♯11 harmony and modern, floating major sounds.
lo.finger_mixolydian_is_a_major_mode_with_a: Mixolydian is a major mode with a ♭7. The major 3rd and ♭7 clearly outline dominant function.
lo.finger_use_it_over_dominant_seventh_harm: Use it over dominant-seventh harmony, blues, rock, funk and Mixolydian progressions.
lo.finger_aeolian_is_the_natural_minor_scal: Aeolian is the natural minor scale. Its ♭6 is an important contrast with Dorian.
lo.finger_use_it_over_minor_harmony_natural: Use it over minor harmony, natural-minor progressions and stable, darker melodies.
lo.finger_locrian_is_a_minor_mode_with_a_5_: Locrian is a minor mode with a ♭5 and ♭2, so its tonic harmony is inherently unstable.
lo.finger_useful_over_m75_half_diminished_h: Useful over m7♭5 (half-diminished) harmony, ear training and highly tense passages.
lo.finger_harmonic_minor_3840b788: ຮາໂມນິກໄມເນີ
lo.finger_harmonic_minor_raises_the_7th_of_: Harmonic minor raises the 7th of natural minor. The ♭6–7 span creates a strong pull to the tonic and its characteristic harmonic colour.
lo.finger_use_it_in_minor_key_harmony_espec: Use it in minor-key harmony, especially V7 resolving to i, as well as classical metal, neoclassical and many flamenco contexts.
lo.finger_melodic_minor_jazz_bcc31317: ເມໂລດິກໄມເນີ (ແຈັດ)
lo.finger_this_is_the_jazz_melodic_minor_fo: This is the jazz melodic-minor form: the same collection ascending and descending. It can be heard as a major scale with a lowered 3rd.
lo.finger_use_it_over_m_maj7_and_m6_harmony: Use it over m(maj7) and m6 harmony and as the parent scale of Lydian dominant, Altered and the other melodic-minor modes.
lo.finger_major_pentatonic_efb6f712: ເພນຕາໂທນິກເມເຈີ
lo.finger_a_bright_accessible_pentatonic_sc: A bright, accessible pentatonic scale with few avoid notes.
lo.finger_useful_for_pop_country_and_soloin: Useful for pop, country and soloing over major chords.
lo.finger_minor_pentatonic_201f7ebd: ເພນຕາໂທນິກໄມເນີ
lo.finger_the_familiar_minor_pentatonic_sou: The familiar minor pentatonic sound used in blues and rock.
lo.finger_useful_for_blues_rock_and_soloing: Useful for blues, rock and soloing over minor chords.
lo.finger_a_variant_formed_by_omitting_degr: A variant formed by omitting degrees 2 and 6 from Mixolydian. “With 4” is shown because methods do not use one universal naming convention.
lo.finger_keeps_the_major_3rd_and_7_and_add: Keeps the major 3rd and ♭7 and adds the 4th; useful over dominant 7, 7sus4, funk and rock.
lo.finger_a_dominant_seventh_outline_plus_d: A dominant-seventh outline plus degree 2/9. Some methods also call it Mixolydian pentatonic.
lo.finger_useful_over_dominant_7_9_harmony_: Useful over dominant 7/9 harmony in jazz, blues and funk, especially when avoiding the 4th.
lo.finger_the_major_blues_scale_is_major_pe: The major blues scale is major pentatonic plus ♭3. The expressive tension between ♭3 and 3 creates its blues colour.
lo.finger_useful_for_major_blues_country_an: Useful for major blues, country and rock and roll over major or dominant harmony, treating ♭3 as a blue note.
lo.finger_the_minor_blues_scale_is_minor_pe: The minor blues scale is minor pentatonic plus ♭5. The ♭5 is its characteristic blue note, often approached or bent toward 5.
lo.finger_useful_for_blues_and_rock_over_mi: Useful for blues and rock over minor or dominant harmony, depending on the harmonic context.
lo.finger_the_second_mode_of_melodic_minor_: The second mode of melodic minor. It keeps Dorian's natural 6th while adding a dark, tense ♭2.
lo.finger_useful_over_m7_9_minor_sus_harmon: Useful over m7(♭9), minor-sus harmony and jazz/fusion passages requiring a darker Dorian colour.
lo.finger_the_third_mode_of_melodic_minor_c: The third mode of melodic minor, combining Lydian's ♯4 with the augmented chord's ♯5.

km.finger_seventh_chords_through_the_circle: អង្កត់ 7 ក្នុងរង្វង់ចតុថ៌
km.finger_lesson_13_has_3_parts_13a_major_1: Lesson 13 has 3 parts: 13A Major → 13B Em7/E7 → 13C Minor
km.finger_roots_on_strings_5_and_2_the_c_ma: Roots on strings 5 and 2; the C-major reference box spans frets 0-3
km.finger_roots_on_strings_5_and_3_the_c_ma: Roots on strings 5 and 3; the C-major reference box spans frets 2-6
km.finger_roots_on_strings_6_3_and_1_the_c_: Roots on strings 6, 3 and 1; the C-major reference box spans frets 5-8
km.finger_roots_on_strings_6_4_and_1_the_c_: Roots on strings 6, 4 and 1; the C-major reference box spans frets 7-10
km.finger_roots_on_strings_4_and_2_the_c_ma: Roots on strings 4 and 2; the C-major reference box spans frets 9-13
km.finger_ionian_is_the_standard_major_scal: Ionian is the standard major scale. Its major 7th creates a strong pull toward the tonic.
km.finger_use_it_over_major_and_maj7_harmon: Use it over major and maj7 harmony and conventional major-key melodies.
km.finger_dorian_is_a_minor_mode_with_a_nat: Dorian is a minor mode with a natural 6th, giving it a brighter sound than Aeolian.
km.finger_useful_over_m7_and_m6_harmony_fun: Useful over m7 and m6 harmony, funk, jazz and Dorian vamps.
km.finger_phrygian_is_a_minor_mode_whose_ch: Phrygian is a minor mode whose characteristic ♭2 creates a dark, tense pull near the tonic.
km.finger_useful_over_static_minor_harmony_: Useful over static minor harmony, metal and Spanish-flavoured lines; it is not the same as Phrygian dominant.
km.finger_lydian_is_a_major_mode_with_a_cha: Lydian is a major mode with a characteristic ♯4, producing a bright and open sound.
km.finger_useful_over_maj7_and_maj711_harmo: Useful over maj7 and maj7♯11 harmony and modern, floating major sounds.
km.finger_mixolydian_is_a_major_mode_with_a: Mixolydian is a major mode with a ♭7. The major 3rd and ♭7 clearly outline dominant function.
km.finger_use_it_over_dominant_seventh_harm: Use it over dominant-seventh harmony, blues, rock, funk and Mixolydian progressions.
km.finger_aeolian_is_the_natural_minor_scal: Aeolian is the natural minor scale. Its ♭6 is an important contrast with Dorian.
km.finger_use_it_over_minor_harmony_natural: Use it over minor harmony, natural-minor progressions and stable, darker melodies.
km.finger_locrian_is_a_minor_mode_with_a_5_: Locrian is a minor mode with a ♭5 and ♭2, so its tonic harmony is inherently unstable.
km.finger_useful_over_m75_half_diminished_h: Useful over m7♭5 (half-diminished) harmony, ear training and highly tense passages.
km.finger_harmonic_minor_3840b788: ម៉ាយន័រហាម៉ូនិក
km.finger_harmonic_minor_raises_the_7th_of_: Harmonic minor raises the 7th of natural minor. The ♭6–7 span creates a strong pull to the tonic and its characteristic harmonic colour.
km.finger_use_it_in_minor_key_harmony_espec: Use it in minor-key harmony, especially V7 resolving to i, as well as classical metal, neoclassical and many flamenco contexts.
km.finger_melodic_minor_jazz_bcc31317: ម៉ាយន័រមេឡូឌិក (ជាស)
km.finger_this_is_the_jazz_melodic_minor_fo: This is the jazz melodic-minor form: the same collection ascending and descending. It can be heard as a major scale with a lowered 3rd.
km.finger_use_it_over_m_maj7_and_m6_harmony: Use it over m(maj7) and m6 harmony and as the parent scale of Lydian dominant, Altered and the other melodic-minor modes.
km.finger_major_pentatonic_efb6f712: ប៉ង់តាតូនិកមេជ័រ
km.finger_a_bright_accessible_pentatonic_sc: A bright, accessible pentatonic scale with few avoid notes.
km.finger_useful_for_pop_country_and_soloin: Useful for pop, country and soloing over major chords.
km.finger_minor_pentatonic_201f7ebd: ប៉ង់តាតូនិកម៉ាយន័រ
km.finger_the_familiar_minor_pentatonic_sou: The familiar minor pentatonic sound used in blues and rock.
km.finger_useful_for_blues_rock_and_soloing: Useful for blues, rock and soloing over minor chords.
km.finger_a_variant_formed_by_omitting_degr: A variant formed by omitting degrees 2 and 6 from Mixolydian. “With 4” is shown because methods do not use one universal naming convention.
km.finger_keeps_the_major_3rd_and_7_and_add: Keeps the major 3rd and ♭7 and adds the 4th; useful over dominant 7, 7sus4, funk and rock.
km.finger_a_dominant_seventh_outline_plus_d: A dominant-seventh outline plus degree 2/9. Some methods also call it Mixolydian pentatonic.
km.finger_useful_over_dominant_7_9_harmony_: Useful over dominant 7/9 harmony in jazz, blues and funk, especially when avoiding the 4th.
km.finger_the_major_blues_scale_is_major_pe: The major blues scale is major pentatonic plus ♭3. The expressive tension between ♭3 and 3 creates its blues colour.
km.finger_useful_for_major_blues_country_an: Useful for major blues, country and rock and roll over major or dominant harmony, treating ♭3 as a blue note.
km.finger_the_minor_blues_scale_is_minor_pe: The minor blues scale is minor pentatonic plus ♭5. The ♭5 is its characteristic blue note, often approached or bent toward 5.
km.finger_useful_for_blues_and_rock_over_mi: Useful for blues and rock over minor or dominant harmony, depending on the harmonic context.
km.finger_the_second_mode_of_melodic_minor_: The second mode of melodic minor. It keeps Dorian's natural 6th while adding a dark, tense ♭2.
km.finger_useful_over_m7_9_minor_sus_harmon: Useful over m7(♭9), minor-sus harmony and jazz/fusion passages requiring a darker Dorian colour.
km.finger_the_third_mode_of_melodic_minor_c: The third mode of melodic minor, combining Lydian's ♯4 with the augmented chord's ♯5.
km.finger_use_it_over_maj75_maj7115_and_mod: Use it over maj7♯5, maj7♯11♯5 and modern augmented-major harmony.
km.finger_the_fourth_mode_of_melodic_minor_: The fourth mode of melodic minor, also called Lydian ♭7. It combines ♯4/♯11 with the dominant major 3rd and ♭7.

ko.finger_roots_on_strings_5_and_2_the_c_ma: Roots on strings 5 and 2; the C-major reference box spans frets 0-3
ko.finger_roots_on_strings_5_and_3_the_c_ma: Roots on strings 5 and 3; the C-major reference box spans frets 2-6
ko.finger_roots_on_strings_6_3_and_1_the_c_: Roots on strings 6, 3 and 1; the C-major reference box spans frets 5-8
ko.finger_roots_on_strings_6_4_and_1_the_c_: Roots on strings 6, 4 and 1; the C-major reference box spans frets 7-10

ko.finger_ionian_is_the_standard_major_scal: Ionian is the standard major scale. Its major 7th creates a strong pull toward the tonic.
ko.finger_use_it_over_major_and_maj7_harmon: Use it over major and maj7 harmony and conventional major-key melodies.
ko.finger_dorian_is_a_minor_mode_with_a_nat: Dorian is a minor mode with a natural 6th, giving it a brighter sound than Aeolian.
ko.finger_useful_over_m7_and_m6_harmony_fun: Useful over m7 and m6 harmony, funk, jazz and Dorian vamps.
ko.finger_phrygian_is_a_minor_mode_whose_ch: Phrygian is a minor mode whose characteristic ♭2 creates a dark, tense pull near the tonic.
ko.finger_useful_over_static_minor_harmony_: Useful over static minor harmony, metal and Spanish-flavoured lines; it is not the same as Phrygian dominant.
ko.finger_lydian_is_a_major_mode_with_a_cha: Lydian is a major mode with a characteristic ♯4, producing a bright and open sound.
ko.finger_useful_over_maj7_and_maj711_harmo: Useful over maj7 and maj7♯11 harmony and modern, floating major sounds.
ko.finger_mixolydian_is_a_major_mode_with_a: Mixolydian is a major mode with a ♭7. The major 3rd and ♭7 clearly outline dominant function.
ko.finger_use_it_over_dominant_seventh_harm: Use it over dominant-seventh harmony, blues, rock, funk and Mixolydian progressions.
ko.finger_aeolian_is_the_natural_minor_scal: Aeolian is the natural minor scale. Its ♭6 is an important contrast with Dorian.
ko.finger_use_it_over_minor_harmony_natural: Use it over minor harmony, natural-minor progressions and stable, darker melodies.
ko.finger_locrian_is_a_minor_mode_with_a_5_: Locrian is a minor mode with a ♭5 and ♭2, so its tonic harmony is inherently unstable.
ko.finger_useful_over_m75_half_diminished_h: Useful over m7♭5 (half-diminished) harmony, ear training and highly tense passages.
ko.finger_harmonic_minor_raises_the_7th_of_: Harmonic minor raises the 7th of natural minor. The ♭6–7 span creates a strong pull to the tonic and its characteristic harmonic colour.
ko.finger_use_it_in_minor_key_harmony_espec: Use it in minor-key harmony, especially V7 resolving to i, as well as classical metal, neoclassical and many flamenco contexts.
ko.finger_this_is_the_jazz_melodic_minor_fo: This is the jazz melodic-minor form: the same collection ascending and descending. It can be heard as a major scale with a lowered 3rd.
ko.finger_use_it_over_m_maj7_and_m6_harmony: Use it over m(maj7) and m6 harmony and as the parent scale of Lydian dominant, Altered and the other melodic-minor modes.
ko.finger_a_bright_accessible_pentatonic_sc: A bright, accessible pentatonic scale with few avoid notes.
ko.finger_useful_for_pop_country_and_soloin: Useful for pop, country and soloing over major chords.
ko.finger_the_familiar_minor_pentatonic_sou: The familiar minor pentatonic sound used in blues and rock.
ko.finger_useful_for_blues_rock_and_soloing: Useful for blues, rock and soloing over minor chords.
ko.finger_a_variant_formed_by_omitting_degr: A variant formed by omitting degrees 2 and 6 from Mixolydian. “With 4” is shown because methods do not use one universal naming convention.
ko.finger_keeps_the_major_3rd_and_7_and_add: Keeps the major 3rd and ♭7 and adds the 4th; useful over dominant 7, 7sus4, funk and rock.
ko.finger_a_dominant_seventh_outline_plus_d: A dominant-seventh outline plus degree 2/9. Some methods also call it Mixolydian pentatonic.
ko.finger_useful_over_dominant_7_9_harmony_: Useful over dominant 7/9 harmony in jazz, blues and funk, especially when avoiding the 4th.
ko.finger_the_major_blues_scale_is_major_pe: The major blues scale is major pentatonic plus ♭3. The expressive tension between ♭3 and 3 creates its blues colour.
ko.finger_useful_for_major_blues_country_an: Useful for major blues, country and rock and roll over major or dominant harmony, treating ♭3 as a blue note.
ko.finger_the_minor_blues_scale_is_minor_pe: The minor blues scale is minor pentatonic plus ♭5. The ♭5 is its characteristic blue note, often approached or bent toward 5.
ko.finger_useful_for_blues_and_rock_over_mi: Useful for blues and rock over minor or dominant harmony, depending on the harmonic context.
ko.finger_the_second_mode_of_melodic_minor_: The second mode of melodic minor. It keeps Dorian's natural 6th while adding a dark, tense ♭2.
ko.finger_useful_over_m7_9_minor_sus_harmon: Useful over m7(♭9), minor-sus harmony and jazz/fusion passages requiring a darker Dorian colour.
ko.finger_the_third_mode_of_melodic_minor_c: The third mode of melodic minor, combining Lydian's ♯4 with the augmented chord's ♯5.
ko.finger_use_it_over_maj75_maj7115_and_mod: Use it over maj7♯5, maj7♯11♯5 and modern augmented-major harmony.
ko.finger_the_fourth_mode_of_melodic_minor_: The fourth mode of melodic minor, also called Lydian ♭7. It combines ♯4/♯11 with the dominant major 3rd and ♭7.
ko.finger_use_it_over_711_chords_non_resolv: Use it over 7♯11 chords, non-resolving dominants, jazz and fusion.
ko.finger_the_fifth_mode_of_melodic_minor_i: The fifth mode of melodic minor. It is Mixolydian with a ♭6, producing a darker dominant sound with a minor inflection.
ko.finger_use_it_over_7_13_dominants_resolv: Use it over 7(♭13), dominants resolving to minor and cinematic dominant harmony.
ko.finger_the_sixth_mode_of_melodic_minor_c: The sixth mode of melodic minor. Compared with ordinary Locrian, its natural 2nd softens the tension next to the tonic.
ko.finger_use_it_over_m75_when_a_natural_9_: Use it over m7♭5 when a natural 9 fits the harmony, especially in minor jazz ii–V–i progressions.
ko.finger_the_seventh_mode_of_melodic_minor: The seventh mode of melodic minor. Beyond 1, 3 and ♭7, it contains the altered dominant tensions ♭9, ♯9, ♭5/♯11 and ♭13.
ko.finger_use_it_over_7alt_79_79_75_or_713_: Use it over 7alt, 7♭9, 7♯9, 7♭5 or 7♭13 when a dominant chord requires strong resolution.
ko.finger_the_second_mode_of_harmonic_minor: The second mode of harmonic minor. It keeps Locrian's ♭2 and ♭5 while raising ♭6 to a natural 6th.
ko.finger_use_it_over_m75_when_a_natural_13: Use it over m7♭5 when a natural 13 fits, or for a brighter half-diminished colour than ordinary Locrian.
ko.finger_the_third_mode_of_harmonic_minor_: The third mode of harmonic minor. It is Ionian with a ♯5, creating a maj7♯5 tonic while retaining a natural 4th.
ko.finger_use_it_over_maj75_and_augmented_m: Use it over maj7♯5 and augmented-major harmony when the natural 4th is preferred to Lydian augmented's ♯4.
ko.finger_the_fourth_mode_of_harmonic_minor: The fourth mode of harmonic minor. It keeps Dorian's natural 6th while replacing the natural 4th with ♯4.
ko.finger_use_it_over_m711_fusion_metal_and: Use it over m7♯11, fusion, metal and minor vamps requiring a brighter yet tenser colour than ordinary Dorian.
ko.finger_the_fifth_mode_of_harmonic_minor_: The fifth mode of harmonic minor. Its ♭2 combined with a major 3rd creates a distinctive dominant sound unlike ordinary Phrygian.
ko.finger_use_it_over_v7_in_minor_keys_9_13: Use it over V7 in minor keys, ♭9/♭13 dominants, metal, fusion and many flamenco contexts.
ko.finger_the_sixth_mode_of_harmonic_minor_: The sixth mode of harmonic minor. It combines ♯2 with Lydian's ♯4, creating an augmented second near the tonic.
ko.finger_use_it_over_maj711_when_a_9_2_fit: Use it over maj7♯11 when a ♯9/♯2 fits the line, mainly in advanced composition and jazz contexts.
ko.finger_the_seventh_mode_of_harmonic_mino: The seventh mode of harmonic minor. It is highly tense, with ♭4, ♭5 and a doubly lowered 7th; it is not the melodic-minor Altered/Super Locrian scale.
ko.finger_use_sparingly_in_composition_dimi: Use sparingly in composition, diminished/altered harmony and advanced ear training; always read it together with its formula.
ko.finger_a_six_note_scale_built_entirely_f: A six-note scale built entirely from whole steps. With no semitones, it sounds floating and unresolved.
ko.finger_use_it_over_augmented_harmony_and: Use it over augmented harmony and dominant chords with ♯5/♭5 for an ambiguous, symmetrical colour.
ko.finger_an_eight_note_symmetrical_scale_a: An eight-note symmetrical scale alternating half and whole steps. It contains a dominant chord plus several altered tensions.
ko.finger_use_it_over_79_79_139_and_dominan: Use it over 7♭9, 7♯9, 13♭9 and dominant-diminished harmony, especially before resolution.
ko.finger_an_eight_note_symmetrical_scale_a: An eight-note symmetrical scale alternating whole and half steps. It outlines a diminished-seventh chord from the tonic.
ko.finger_use_it_over_7_harmony_diminished_: Use it over °7 harmony, diminished sequences and minor-third transposition practice.
ko.finger_the_chromatic_scale_contains_all_: The chromatic scale contains all 12 pitch classes in the octave. It is not a major-scale mode but the complete semitone collection.
ko.finger_use_it_for_technique_chromatic_ap: Use it for technique, chromatic approaches between chord tones, semitone ear training and chromatic line development.
ko.finger_mixolydian_plus_a_major_7th_passi: Mixolydian plus a major 7th passing tone. With suitable rhythmic placement, chord tones can align consistently with strong beats.
ko.finger_use_it_over_dominant_seventh_harm: Use it over dominant-seventh harmony in bebop and jazz; practise it rhythmically rather than only as a mechanical up-and-down scale.
ko.finger_a_major_scale_with_a_lowered_6th_: A major scale with a lowered 6th, combining a major tonic with the ♭6 colour often associated with minor harmony.
ko.finger_use_it_over_maj7_13_borrowed_harm: Use it over maj7(♭13), borrowed harmony and major-key lines requiring a darker colour.
ko.finger_a_major_scale_with_2_and_6_creati: A major scale with ♭2 and ♭6, creating two characteristic augmented seconds. Some Western sources also call it Byzantine.
ko.finger_use_it_for_western_labelled_middl: Use it for Western-labelled Middle Eastern/Mediterranean colours, metal, fusion and composition requiring strong tension.
ko.finger_ritusen_yo_pentatonic_mode_12456_: Ritusen/Yo pentatonic mode: 1–2–4–5–6. With G as tonic, G–A–C–D–E shares the pitches of C major pentatonic, so its open C-reference shape is valid while G stays the root (R). This differs from dominant 1–3–4–5–b7.
ko.finger_use_for_open_suspended_pentatonic: Use for open/suspended pentatonic sounds. In G, the C-major reference shape occupies open strings through fret 4; keep G as the tonal centre.
ko.finger_tuner_tools_uses_the_common_weste: Tuner Tools uses the common Western reference form 1–2–♭3–5–♭6. Naming and pitches can vary with tuning, instrument and Japanese tradition.
ko.finger_useful_for_pentatonic_melody_writ: Useful for pentatonic melody writing with wide gaps, a dark colour and interval-control practice.
ko.finger_the_western_reference_form_12457_: The Western reference form 1–♭2–4–5–♭7 creates a dark suspended colour. Traditional terminology can vary by source and tuning.
ko.finger_useful_over_sus_harmony_dark_melo: Useful over sus harmony, dark melody, ambient, metal and exercises emphasizing the ♭2.
ko.finger_the_western_reference_form_12457_: The Western reference form 1–♭2–4–♭5–♭7 has strongly tense ♭2 and ♭5 degrees. Its historical name should not be treated as one absolutely fixed Western mode.
ko.finger_useful_for_dark_melody_sound_desi: Useful for dark melody, sound design, metal and ear training with tense intervals.
ko.finger_a_custom_roman_numeral_loop_that_: A custom Roman-numeral loop that is saved automatically and transposes to every key.
ko.finger_the_dominant_of_the_target_chord_: The dominant of the target chord; its 3rd and 7th pull clearly into {0}.
ko.finger_the_diminished_chord_root_lies_a_: The diminished chord root lies a semitone below {0}, resolving upward into the destination root.
ko.finger_a_dominant_a_semitone_above_the_t: A dominant a semitone above the target, useful in jazz with a strong chromatic bass line.
ko.finger_keep_the_hand_relaxed_and_play_1_: Keep the hand relaxed and play 1-2-3-4 evenly across six strings.
ko.finger_each_finger_owns_one_fret_alterna: Each finger owns one fret; alternate picking synchronizes both hands.
ko.finger_apply_the_same_pulse_to_a_short_c: Apply the same pulse to a short chromatic line.
ko.finger_change_strings_without_breaking_t: Change strings without breaking the pulse and keep the picking motion compact.
ko.finger_alternate_picking_continues_throu: Alternate picking continues through string changes instead of restarting on each string.
ko.finger_use_this_motion_in_riffs_and_mult: Use this motion in riffs and multi-string solo lines.
ko.finger_separate_each_finger_movement_esp: Separate each finger movement, especially fingers 3 and 4.
ko.finger_lift_only_the_moving_finger_and_k: Lift only the moving finger and keep the others close to the strings.
ko.finger_prepare_for_scale_and_arpeggio_li: Prepare for scale and arpeggio lines with changing finger order.
ko.finger_keep_planted_fingers_down_while_t: Keep planted fingers down while the next finger crosses to the adjacent string.
ko.finger_the_spider_drill_develops_finger_: The Spider drill develops finger independence and two-hand string control.
ko.finger_useful_for_chords_legato_and_diag: Useful for chords, legato and diagonal string-crossing lines.
ko.finger_keep_an_even_pulse_between_1_2_3_: Keep an even pulse between 1-2-3 and 2-3-4 groups.
ko.finger_sequences_create_musical_phrasing: Sequences create musical phrasing instead of merely running straight up and down.
ko.finger_use_three_note_groups_to_build_sc: Use three-note groups to build scale-based solo phrases.
ko.finger_produce_even_notes_with_the_frett: Produce even notes with the fretting hand without repicking every note.
ko.finger_pick_the_first_note_then_articula: Pick the first note, then articulate with the fretting hand while staying in time.
ko.finger_apply_it_to_legato_phrases_and_po: Apply it to legato phrases and position connections.
ko.finger_hear_and_see_the_root_third_and_f: Hear and see the root, third and fifth through an I-IV-V progression.
ko.finger_the_third_defines_major_or_minor_: The third defines major or minor quality; the fifth adds stability.
ko.finger_play_c_f_g_on_strings_1_2_3_with_: Play C-F-G on strings 1-2-3 with an even pulse.
ko.finger_recognize_root_position_first_and: Recognize root position, first and second inversion in one fretboard area.
ko.finger_the_lowest_note_determines_the_in: The lowest note determines the inversion while the three chord tones remain the same.
ko.finger_connect_i_iv_v_with_the_nearest_i: Connect I-IV-V with the nearest inversion instead of large position jumps.
ko.finger_play_i_ii_iii_iv_v_vi_vii_and_rec: Play I-ii-iii-IV-V-vi-vii° and recognize root, first and second inversion on strings 1-2-3.
ko.finger_in_every_major_key_the_seven_tria: In every major key, the seven triads follow: Major-Minor-Minor-Major-Major-Minor-Diminished.
ko.finger_in_c_c_dm_em_f_g_am_bdim_this_map: In C: C-Dm-Em-F-G-Am-Bdim; this map supports accompaniment, analysis and progression building.
ko.finger_connect_dm_g_c_with_minimal_hand_: Connect Dm-G-C with minimal hand movement.
ko.finger_ii_prepares_v_creates_tension_and: ii prepares, V creates tension and I provides resolution.
ko.finger_use_it_in_ballads_jazz_and_chord_: Use it in ballads, jazz and chord-tone soloing.
ko.finger_connect_i_v_vi_iv_using_common_to: Connect I-V-vi-IV using common tones and nearest inversions.
ko.finger_retaining_common_tones_smooths_ch: Retaining common tones smooths chord changes and reduces unnecessary motion.
ko.finger_apply_it_directly_to_modern_pop_a: Apply it directly to modern pop and ballad accompaniment.
ko.finger_play_dm7_g7_cmaj7_and_hear_the_co: Play Dm7-G7-Cmaj7 and hear the color of each seventh.
ko.finger_the_third_and_seventh_are_guide_t: The third and seventh are guide tones that reveal harmonic function.
ko.finger_resolve_phrases_to_the_third_or_s: Resolve phrases to the third or seventh over a ii-V-I.
ko.finger_run_cmaj7_fmaj7_bm75_em7_am7_dm7_: Run Cmaj7-Fmaj7-Bm7♭5-Em7-Am7-Dm7-G7 and hear G7 resolve to Cmaj7.
ko.finger_these_are_the_seven_diatonic_seve: These are the seven diatonic seventh chords of C major, ordered by fourths for function and voice-leading.
ko.finger_use_this_cycle_for_harmonic_analy: Use this cycle for harmonic analysis, guide-tone practice and smooth jazz/pop changes.
ko.finger_compare_em7am7_with_e7am7_and_hea: Compare Em7→Am7 with E7→Am7 and hear G rise to G#, creating a pull toward A.
ko.finger_em7_belongs_to_a_natural_minor_e7: Em7 belongs to A natural minor; E7 borrows G# from A harmonic minor to become the dominant V7.
ko.finger_hear_and_see_both_resolutions_to_: Hear and see both resolutions to understand why E7→Am is stronger than Em7→Am.
ko.finger_combine_seventh_chord_arpeggios_v: Combine seventh-chord arpeggios, voice-leading and harmonic minor through Am7-Dm7-G7-Cmaj7-Fmaj7-Bm7♭5-E7.
ko.finger_e7_uses_g_from_harmonic_minor_to_: E7 uses G# from harmonic minor to pull strongly back to Am.
ko.finger_apply_it_to_jazz_turnarounds_stan: Apply it to jazz turnarounds, standards and key movement.
ko.finger_scale_order_i_ii_iii_iv_v_vi_vii_: Scale order I-ii-iii-IV-V-vi-vii°: C-Dm-Em-F-G-Am-Bdim in C major.
ko.finger_diatonic_1473625_cfbdimemamdmg_in: Diatonic 1–4–7–3–6–2–5: C–F–Bdim–Em–Am–Dm–G in C; resolves to I.
ko.finger_a_minor_compare_em7am7_natural_mi: A minor: compare Em7→Am7 (natural minor) with E7→Am7 (harmonic minor, G# leading to A).
ko.finger_the_classic_jazz_cadence_for_targ: The classic jazz cadence for target notes and harmonic resolution.
ko.finger_a_foundation_of_pop_rock_blues_an: A foundation of pop, rock, blues and folk.
ko.finger_a_modern_pop_ballad_loop_ideal_fo: A modern pop/ballad loop ideal for connected positions.
ko.finger_a_common_turnaround_in_jazz_balla: A common turnaround in jazz, ballads and standards.
ko.finger_the_classic_1_6_4_5_loop_for_acco: The classic 1-6-4-5 loop for accompaniment and chord changes.
ko.finger_a_minor_2_5_1_with_half_diminishe: A minor 2-5-1 with half-diminished ii and a strong V7 pull.
ko.finger_a_familiar_minor_key_loop_in_rock: A familiar minor-key loop in rock, pop and cinematic music.
ko.finger_a_basic_minor_functional_cadence_: A basic minor functional cadence with a major V resolving to i.
ko.finger_twelve_bars_of_i7_iv7_v7_for_groo: Twelve bars of I7-IV7-V7 for groove and dominant arpeggios.
ko.finger_pattern_1_2_3_4_on_each_string_re: 각 줄 1-2-3-4 패턴 · 첫 연습 추천
ko.finger_coordinate_both_hands_while_movin: 줄 이동 중 양손을 맞춰 연습
ko.finger_move_only_the_required_finger_wit: 손 전체를 들지 말고 필요한 손가락만 움직이세요.
ko.finger_keep_planted_fingers_down_and_mov: 누른 손가락을 유지하고 다음 손가락만 움직이세요.
ko.finger_keep_an_even_pulse_between_the_1_: Keep an even pulse between the 1-2-3 and 2-3-4 groups.
ko.finger_a_left_hand_technique_for_after_t: 네 손가락 제어 후 익히는 왼손 테크닉
ko.finger_pick_the_first_note_then_use_the_: Pick the first note, then use the fretting hand while keeping steady time.
ko.finger_plant_one_or_two_fingers_move_the: 한두 손가락을 고정하고 나머지를 한 줄에서 움직입니다.
ko.finger_keep_the_anchored_fingers_down_ch: 고정 손가락을 유지하고 한두 개를 선택해 천천히 편하게 연주하세요.
ko.finger_anchor_one_or_two_fingers_move_th: 한두 손가락을 고정하고 나머지를 인접 두 줄 사이로 이동합니다.

ko.finger_harmony_colours_are_calculated_ag: Harmony colours are calculated against the tonic triad: blue marks chord tones; green marks the remaining matching pentatonic tones; gold marks colour tensions; red marks strong tensions that commonly resolve to a nearby tone. In A Aeolian over Am: A–C–E are blue, D–G green, B gold and F red.

pt.finger_lesson_13_has_3_parts_13a_major_1: Lesson 13 has 3 parts: 13A Major → 13B Em7/E7 → 13C Minor
pt.finger_roots_on_strings_5_and_2_the_c_ma: Roots on strings 5 and 2; the C-major reference box spans frets 0-3
pt.finger_roots_on_strings_5_and_3_the_c_ma: Roots on strings 5 and 3; the C-major reference box spans frets 2-6
pt.finger_roots_on_strings_6_3_and_1_the_c_: Roots on strings 6, 3 and 1; the C-major reference box spans frets 5-8
pt.finger_roots_on_strings_6_4_and_1_the_c_: Roots on strings 6, 4 and 1; the C-major reference box spans frets 7-10

pt.finger_ionian_is_the_standard_major_scal: Ionian is the standard major scale. Its major 7th creates a strong pull toward the tonic.
pt.finger_use_it_over_major_and_maj7_harmon: Use it over major and maj7 harmony and conventional major-key melodies.
pt.finger_dorian_is_a_minor_mode_with_a_nat: Dorian is a minor mode with a natural 6th, giving it a brighter sound than Aeolian.
pt.finger_useful_over_m7_and_m6_harmony_fun: Useful over m7 and m6 harmony, funk, jazz and Dorian vamps.
pt.finger_phrygian_is_a_minor_mode_whose_ch: Phrygian is a minor mode whose characteristic ♭2 creates a dark, tense pull near the tonic.
pt.finger_useful_over_static_minor_harmony_: Useful over static minor harmony, metal and Spanish-flavoured lines; it is not the same as Phrygian dominant.
pt.finger_lydian_is_a_major_mode_with_a_cha: Lydian is a major mode with a characteristic ♯4, producing a bright and open sound.
pt.finger_useful_over_maj7_and_maj711_harmo: Useful over maj7 and maj7♯11 harmony and modern, floating major sounds.
pt.finger_mixolydian_is_a_major_mode_with_a: Mixolydian is a major mode with a ♭7. The major 3rd and ♭7 clearly outline dominant function.
pt.finger_use_it_over_dominant_seventh_harm: Use it over dominant-seventh harmony, blues, rock, funk and Mixolydian progressions.
pt.finger_aeolian_is_the_natural_minor_scal: Aeolian is the natural minor scale. Its ♭6 is an important contrast with Dorian.
pt.finger_use_it_over_minor_harmony_natural: Use it over minor harmony, natural-minor progressions and stable, darker melodies.
pt.finger_locrian_is_a_minor_mode_with_a_5_: Locrian is a minor mode with a ♭5 and ♭2, so its tonic harmony is inherently unstable.
pt.finger_useful_over_m75_half_diminished_h: Useful over m7♭5 (half-diminished) harmony, ear training and highly tense passages.
pt.finger_harmonic_minor_raises_the_7th_of_: Harmonic minor raises the 7th of natural minor. The ♭6–7 span creates a strong pull to the tonic and its characteristic harmonic colour.
pt.finger_use_it_in_minor_key_harmony_espec: Use it in minor-key harmony, especially V7 resolving to i, as well as classical metal, neoclassical and many flamenco contexts.
pt.finger_this_is_the_jazz_melodic_minor_fo: This is the jazz melodic-minor form: the same collection ascending and descending. It can be heard as a major scale with a lowered 3rd.
pt.finger_use_it_over_m_maj7_and_m6_harmony: Use it over m(maj7) and m6 harmony and as the parent scale of Lydian dominant, Altered and the other melodic-minor modes.
pt.finger_a_bright_accessible_pentatonic_sc: A bright, accessible pentatonic scale with few avoid notes.
pt.finger_useful_for_pop_country_and_soloin: Useful for pop, country and soloing over major chords.
pt.finger_the_familiar_minor_pentatonic_sou: The familiar minor pentatonic sound used in blues and rock.
pt.finger_useful_for_blues_rock_and_soloing: Useful for blues, rock and soloing over minor chords.
pt.finger_a_variant_formed_by_omitting_degr: A variant formed by omitting degrees 2 and 6 from Mixolydian. “With 4” is shown because methods do not use one universal naming convention.
pt.finger_keeps_the_major_3rd_and_7_and_add: Keeps the major 3rd and ♭7 and adds the 4th; useful over dominant 7, 7sus4, funk and rock.
pt.finger_a_dominant_seventh_outline_plus_d: A dominant-seventh outline plus degree 2/9. Some methods also call it Mixolydian pentatonic.
pt.finger_useful_over_dominant_7_9_harmony_: Useful over dominant 7/9 harmony in jazz, blues and funk, especially when avoiding the 4th.
pt.finger_the_major_blues_scale_is_major_pe: The major blues scale is major pentatonic plus ♭3. The expressive tension between ♭3 and 3 creates its blues colour.
pt.finger_useful_for_major_blues_country_an: Useful for major blues, country and rock and roll over major or dominant harmony, treating ♭3 as a blue note.
pt.finger_the_minor_blues_scale_is_minor_pe: The minor blues scale is minor pentatonic plus ♭5. The ♭5 is its characteristic blue note, often approached or bent toward 5.
pt.finger_useful_for_blues_and_rock_over_mi: Useful for blues and rock over minor or dominant harmony, depending on the harmonic context.
pt.finger_the_second_mode_of_melodic_minor_: The second mode of melodic minor. It keeps Dorian's natural 6th while adding a dark, tense ♭2.
pt.finger_useful_over_m7_9_minor_sus_harmon: Useful over m7(♭9), minor-sus harmony and jazz/fusion passages requiring a darker Dorian colour.
pt.finger_the_third_mode_of_melodic_minor_c: The third mode of melodic minor, combining Lydian's ♯4 with the augmented chord's ♯5.
pt.finger_use_it_over_maj75_maj7115_and_mod: Use it over maj7♯5, maj7♯11♯5 and modern augmented-major harmony.
pt.finger_the_fourth_mode_of_melodic_minor_: The fourth mode of melodic minor, also called Lydian ♭7. It combines ♯4/♯11 with the dominant major 3rd and ♭7.
pt.finger_use_it_over_711_chords_non_resolv: Use it over 7♯11 chords, non-resolving dominants, jazz and fusion.
pt.finger_the_fifth_mode_of_melodic_minor_i: The fifth mode of melodic minor. It is Mixolydian with a ♭6, producing a darker dominant sound with a minor inflection.
pt.finger_use_it_over_7_13_dominants_resolv: Use it over 7(♭13), dominants resolving to minor and cinematic dominant harmony.
pt.finger_the_sixth_mode_of_melodic_minor_c: The sixth mode of melodic minor. Compared with ordinary Locrian, its natural 2nd softens the tension next to the tonic.
pt.finger_use_it_over_m75_when_a_natural_9_: Use it over m7♭5 when a natural 9 fits the harmony, especially in minor jazz ii–V–i progressions.
pt.finger_the_seventh_mode_of_melodic_minor: The seventh mode of melodic minor. Beyond 1, 3 and ♭7, it contains the altered dominant tensions ♭9, ♯9, ♭5/♯11 and ♭13.
pt.finger_use_it_over_7alt_79_79_75_or_713_: Use it over 7alt, 7♭9, 7♯9, 7♭5 or 7♭13 when a dominant chord requires strong resolution.
pt.finger_the_second_mode_of_harmonic_minor: The second mode of harmonic minor. It keeps Locrian's ♭2 and ♭5 while raising ♭6 to a natural 6th.
pt.finger_use_it_over_m75_when_a_natural_13: Use it over m7♭5 when a natural 13 fits, or for a brighter half-diminished colour than ordinary Locrian.
pt.finger_the_third_mode_of_harmonic_minor_: The third mode of harmonic minor. It is Ionian with a ♯5, creating a maj7♯5 tonic while retaining a natural 4th.
pt.finger_use_it_over_maj75_and_augmented_m: Use it over maj7♯5 and augmented-major harmony when the natural 4th is preferred to Lydian augmented's ♯4.
pt.finger_the_fourth_mode_of_harmonic_minor: The fourth mode of harmonic minor. It keeps Dorian's natural 6th while replacing the natural 4th with ♯4.
pt.finger_use_it_over_m711_fusion_metal_and: Use it over m7♯11, fusion, metal and minor vamps requiring a brighter yet tenser colour than ordinary Dorian.
pt.finger_the_fifth_mode_of_harmonic_minor_: The fifth mode of harmonic minor. Its ♭2 combined with a major 3rd creates a distinctive dominant sound unlike ordinary Phrygian.
pt.finger_use_it_over_v7_in_minor_keys_9_13: Use it over V7 in minor keys, ♭9/♭13 dominants, metal, fusion and many flamenco contexts.
pt.finger_the_sixth_mode_of_harmonic_minor_: The sixth mode of harmonic minor. It combines ♯2 with Lydian's ♯4, creating an augmented second near the tonic.
pt.finger_use_it_over_maj711_when_a_9_2_fit: Use it over maj7♯11 when a ♯9/♯2 fits the line, mainly in advanced composition and jazz contexts.
pt.finger_the_seventh_mode_of_harmonic_mino: The seventh mode of harmonic minor. It is highly tense, with ♭4, ♭5 and a doubly lowered 7th; it is not the melodic-minor Altered/Super Locrian scale.
pt.finger_use_sparingly_in_composition_dimi: Use sparingly in composition, diminished/altered harmony and advanced ear training; always read it together with its formula.
pt.finger_a_six_note_scale_built_entirely_f: A six-note scale built entirely from whole steps. With no semitones, it sounds floating and unresolved.
pt.finger_use_it_over_augmented_harmony_and: Use it over augmented harmony and dominant chords with ♯5/♭5 for an ambiguous, symmetrical colour.
pt.finger_an_eight_note_symmetrical_scale_a: An eight-note symmetrical scale alternating half and whole steps. It contains a dominant chord plus several altered tensions.
pt.finger_use_it_over_79_79_139_and_dominan: Use it over 7♭9, 7♯9, 13♭9 and dominant-diminished harmony, especially before resolution.
pt.finger_an_eight_note_symmetrical_scale_a: An eight-note symmetrical scale alternating whole and half steps. It outlines a diminished-seventh chord from the tonic.
pt.finger_use_it_over_7_harmony_diminished_: Use it over °7 harmony, diminished sequences and minor-third transposition practice.
pt.finger_the_chromatic_scale_contains_all_: The chromatic scale contains all 12 pitch classes in the octave. It is not a major-scale mode but the complete semitone collection.
pt.finger_use_it_for_technique_chromatic_ap: Use it for technique, chromatic approaches between chord tones, semitone ear training and chromatic line development.
pt.finger_mixolydian_plus_a_major_7th_passi: Mixolydian plus a major 7th passing tone. With suitable rhythmic placement, chord tones can align consistently with strong beats.
pt.finger_use_it_over_dominant_seventh_harm: Use it over dominant-seventh harmony in bebop and jazz; practise it rhythmically rather than only as a mechanical up-and-down scale.
pt.finger_a_major_scale_with_a_lowered_6th_: A major scale with a lowered 6th, combining a major tonic with the ♭6 colour often associated with minor harmony.
pt.finger_use_it_over_maj7_13_borrowed_harm: Use it over maj7(♭13), borrowed harmony and major-key lines requiring a darker colour.
pt.finger_a_major_scale_with_2_and_6_creati: A major scale with ♭2 and ♭6, creating two characteristic augmented seconds. Some Western sources also call it Byzantine.
pt.finger_use_it_for_western_labelled_middl: Use it for Western-labelled Middle Eastern/Mediterranean colours, metal, fusion and composition requiring strong tension.
pt.finger_ritusen_yo_pentatonic_mode_12456_: Ritusen/Yo pentatonic mode: 1–2–4–5–6. With G as tonic, G–A–C–D–E shares the pitches of C major pentatonic, so its open C-reference shape is valid while G stays the root (R). This differs from dominant 1–3–4–5–b7.
pt.finger_use_for_open_suspended_pentatonic: Use for open/suspended pentatonic sounds. In G, the C-major reference shape occupies open strings through fret 4; keep G as the tonal centre.
pt.finger_tuner_tools_uses_the_common_weste: Tuner Tools uses the common Western reference form 1–2–♭3–5–♭6. Naming and pitches can vary with tuning, instrument and Japanese tradition.
pt.finger_useful_for_pentatonic_melody_writ: Useful for pentatonic melody writing with wide gaps, a dark colour and interval-control practice.
pt.finger_the_western_reference_form_12457_: The Western reference form 1–♭2–4–5–♭7 creates a dark suspended colour. Traditional terminology can vary by source and tuning.
pt.finger_useful_over_sus_harmony_dark_melo: Useful over sus harmony, dark melody, ambient, metal and exercises emphasizing the ♭2.
pt.finger_the_western_reference_form_12457_: The Western reference form 1–♭2–4–♭5–♭7 has strongly tense ♭2 and ♭5 degrees. Its historical name should not be treated as one absolutely fixed Western mode.
pt.finger_useful_for_dark_melody_sound_desi: Useful for dark melody, sound design, metal and ear training with tense intervals.
pt.finger_a_custom_roman_numeral_loop_that_: A custom Roman-numeral loop that is saved automatically and transposes to every key.
pt.finger_the_dominant_of_the_target_chord_: The dominant of the target chord; its 3rd and 7th pull clearly into {0}.
pt.finger_the_diminished_chord_root_lies_a_: The diminished chord root lies a semitone below {0}, resolving upward into the destination root.
pt.finger_a_dominant_a_semitone_above_the_t: A dominant a semitone above the target, useful in jazz with a strong chromatic bass line.
pt.finger_keep_the_hand_relaxed_and_play_1_: Keep the hand relaxed and play 1-2-3-4 evenly across six strings.
pt.finger_each_finger_owns_one_fret_alterna: Each finger owns one fret; alternate picking synchronizes both hands.
pt.finger_apply_the_same_pulse_to_a_short_c: Apply the same pulse to a short chromatic line.
pt.finger_change_strings_without_breaking_t: Change strings without breaking the pulse and keep the picking motion compact.
pt.finger_alternate_picking_continues_throu: Alternate picking continues through string changes instead of restarting on each string.
pt.finger_use_this_motion_in_riffs_and_mult: Use this motion in riffs and multi-string solo lines.
pt.finger_separate_each_finger_movement_esp: Separate each finger movement, especially fingers 3 and 4.
pt.finger_lift_only_the_moving_finger_and_k: Lift only the moving finger and keep the others close to the strings.
pt.finger_prepare_for_scale_and_arpeggio_li: Prepare for scale and arpeggio lines with changing finger order.
pt.finger_keep_planted_fingers_down_while_t: Keep planted fingers down while the next finger crosses to the adjacent string.
pt.finger_the_spider_drill_develops_finger_: The Spider drill develops finger independence and two-hand string control.
pt.finger_useful_for_chords_legato_and_diag: Useful for chords, legato and diagonal string-crossing lines.
pt.finger_keep_an_even_pulse_between_1_2_3_: Keep an even pulse between 1-2-3 and 2-3-4 groups.
pt.finger_sequences_create_musical_phrasing: Sequences create musical phrasing instead of merely running straight up and down.
pt.finger_use_three_note_groups_to_build_sc: Use three-note groups to build scale-based solo phrases.
pt.finger_produce_even_notes_with_the_frett: Produce even notes with the fretting hand without repicking every note.
pt.finger_pick_the_first_note_then_articula: Pick the first note, then articulate with the fretting hand while staying in time.
pt.finger_apply_it_to_legato_phrases_and_po: Apply it to legato phrases and position connections.
pt.finger_hear_and_see_the_root_third_and_f: Hear and see the root, third and fifth through an I-IV-V progression.
pt.finger_the_third_defines_major_or_minor_: The third defines major or minor quality; the fifth adds stability.
pt.finger_play_c_f_g_on_strings_1_2_3_with_: Play C-F-G on strings 1-2-3 with an even pulse.
pt.finger_recognize_root_position_first_and: Recognize root position, first and second inversion in one fretboard area.
pt.finger_the_lowest_note_determines_the_in: The lowest note determines the inversion while the three chord tones remain the same.
pt.finger_connect_i_iv_v_with_the_nearest_i: Connect I-IV-V with the nearest inversion instead of large position jumps.
pt.finger_triads_seven_chords_in_a_major_ke: Tríades · sete acordes no tom maior
pt.finger_play_i_ii_iii_iv_v_vi_vii_and_rec: Play I-ii-iii-IV-V-vi-vii° and recognize root, first and second inversion on strings 1-2-3.
pt.finger_in_every_major_key_the_seven_tria: In every major key, the seven triads follow: Major-Minor-Minor-Major-Major-Minor-Diminished.
pt.finger_in_c_c_dm_em_f_g_am_bdim_this_map: In C: C-Dm-Em-F-G-Am-Bdim; this map supports accompaniment, analysis and progression building.
pt.finger_connect_dm_g_c_with_minimal_hand_: Connect Dm-G-C with minimal hand movement.
pt.finger_ii_prepares_v_creates_tension_and: ii prepares, V creates tension and I provides resolution.
pt.finger_use_it_in_ballads_jazz_and_chord_: Use it in ballads, jazz and chord-tone soloing.
pt.finger_connect_i_v_vi_iv_using_common_to: Connect I-V-vi-IV using common tones and nearest inversions.
pt.finger_retaining_common_tones_smooths_ch: Retaining common tones smooths chord changes and reduces unnecessary motion.
pt.finger_apply_it_directly_to_modern_pop_a: Apply it directly to modern pop and ballad accompaniment.

pt.finger_play_dm7_g7_cmaj7_and_hear_the_co: Play Dm7-G7-Cmaj7 and hear the color of each seventh.
pt.finger_the_third_and_seventh_are_guide_t: The third and seventh are guide tones that reveal harmonic function.
