ar.finger_lesson_13_has_3_parts_13a_major_1: Lesson 13 has 3 parts: 13A Major → 13B Em7/E7 → 13C Minor
ar.finger_roots_on_strings_5_and_2_the_c_ma: Roots on strings 5 and 2; the C-major reference box spans frets 0-3
ar.finger_roots_on_strings_5_and_3_the_c_ma: Roots on strings 5 and 3; the C-major reference box spans frets 2-6
ar.finger_roots_on_strings_6_3_and_1_the_c_: Roots on strings 6, 3 and 1; the C-major reference box spans frets 5-8
ar.finger_roots_on_strings_6_4_and_1_the_c_: Roots on strings 6, 4 and 1; the C-major reference box spans frets 7-10
ar.finger_roots_on_strings_4_and_2_the_c_ma: Roots on strings 4 and 2; the C-major reference box spans frets 9-13
ar.finger_ionian_is_the_standard_major_scal: Ionian is the standard major scale. Its major 7th creates a strong pull toward the tonic.
ar.finger_use_it_over_major_and_maj7_harmon: Use it over major and maj7 harmony and conventional major-key melodies.
ar.finger_dorian_is_a_minor_mode_with_a_nat: Dorian is a minor mode with a natural 6th, giving it a brighter sound than Aeolian.
ar.finger_useful_over_m7_and_m6_harmony_fun: Useful over m7 and m6 harmony, funk, jazz and Dorian vamps.
ar.finger_phrygian_is_a_minor_mode_whose_ch: Phrygian is a minor mode whose characteristic ♭2 creates a dark, tense pull near the tonic.
ar.finger_useful_over_static_minor_harmony_: Useful over static minor harmony, metal and Spanish-flavoured lines; it is not the same as Phrygian dominant.
ar.finger_lydian_is_a_major_mode_with_a_cha: Lydian is a major mode with a characteristic ♯4, producing a bright and open sound.
ar.finger_useful_over_maj7_and_maj711_harmo: Useful over maj7 and maj7♯11 harmony and modern, floating major sounds.
ar.finger_mixolydian_is_a_major_mode_with_a: Mixolydian is a major mode with a ♭7. The major 3rd and ♭7 clearly outline dominant function.
ar.finger_use_it_over_dominant_seventh_harm: Use it over dominant-seventh harmony, blues, rock, funk and Mixolydian progressions.
ar.finger_aeolian_is_the_natural_minor_scal: Aeolian is the natural minor scale. Its ♭6 is an important contrast with Dorian.
ar.finger_use_it_over_minor_harmony_natural: Use it over minor harmony, natural-minor progressions and stable, darker melodies.
ar.finger_locrian_is_a_minor_mode_with_a_5_: Locrian is a minor mode with a ♭5 and ♭2, so its tonic harmony is inherently unstable.
ar.finger_useful_over_m75_half_diminished_h: Useful over m7♭5 (half-diminished) harmony, ear training and highly tense passages.
ar.finger_harmonic_minor_raises_the_7th_of_: Harmonic minor raises the 7th of natural minor. The ♭6–7 span creates a strong pull to the tonic and its characteristic harmonic colour.
ar.finger_use_it_in_minor_key_harmony_espec: Use it in minor-key harmony, especially V7 resolving to i, as well as classical metal, neoclassical and many flamenco contexts.
ar.finger_this_is_the_jazz_melodic_minor_fo: This is the jazz melodic-minor form: the same collection ascending and descending. It can be heard as a major scale with a lowered 3rd.
ar.finger_use_it_over_m_maj7_and_m6_harmony: Use it over m(maj7) and m6 harmony and as the parent scale of Lydian dominant, Altered and the other melodic-minor modes.
ar.finger_a_bright_accessible_pentatonic_sc: A bright, accessible pentatonic scale with few avoid notes.
ar.finger_useful_for_pop_country_and_soloin: Useful for pop, country and soloing over major chords.
ar.finger_the_familiar_minor_pentatonic_sou: The familiar minor pentatonic sound used in blues and rock.
ar.finger_useful_for_blues_rock_and_soloing: Useful for blues, rock and soloing over minor chords.
ar.finger_a_variant_formed_by_omitting_degr: A variant formed by omitting degrees 2 and 6 from Mixolydian. “With 4” is shown because methods do not use one universal naming convention.
ar.finger_keeps_the_major_3rd_and_7_and_add: Keeps the major 3rd and ♭7 and adds the 4th; useful over dominant 7, 7sus4, funk and rock.
ar.finger_a_dominant_seventh_outline_plus_d: A dominant-seventh outline plus degree 2/9. Some methods also call it Mixolydian pentatonic.
ar.finger_useful_over_dominant_7_9_harmony_: Useful over dominant 7/9 harmony in jazz, blues and funk, especially when avoiding the 4th.
ar.finger_the_major_blues_scale_is_major_pe: The major blues scale is major pentatonic plus ♭3. The expressive tension between ♭3 and 3 creates its blues colour.
ar.finger_useful_for_major_blues_country_an: Useful for major blues, country and rock and roll over major or dominant harmony, treating ♭3 as a blue note.
ar.finger_the_minor_blues_scale_is_minor_pe: The minor blues scale is minor pentatonic plus ♭5. The ♭5 is its characteristic blue note, often approached or bent toward 5.
ar.finger_useful_for_blues_and_rock_over_mi: Useful for blues and rock over minor or dominant harmony, depending on the harmonic context.
ar.finger_the_second_mode_of_melodic_minor_: The second mode of melodic minor. It keeps Dorian's natural 6th while adding a dark, tense ♭2.
ar.finger_useful_over_m7_9_minor_sus_harmon: Useful over m7(♭9), minor-sus harmony and jazz/fusion passages requiring a darker Dorian colour.
ar.finger_the_third_mode_of_melodic_minor_c: The third mode of melodic minor, combining Lydian's ♯4 with the augmented chord's ♯5.
ar.finger_use_it_over_maj75_maj7115_and_mod: Use it over maj7♯5, maj7♯11♯5 and modern augmented-major harmony.
ar.finger_the_fourth_mode_of_melodic_minor_: The fourth mode of melodic minor, also called Lydian ♭7. It combines ♯4/♯11 with the dominant major 3rd and ♭7.
ar.finger_use_it_over_711_chords_non_resolv: Use it over 7♯11 chords, non-resolving dominants, jazz and fusion.
ar.finger_the_fifth_mode_of_melodic_minor_i: The fifth mode of melodic minor. It is Mixolydian with a ♭6, producing a darker dominant sound with a minor inflection.
ar.finger_use_it_over_7_13_dominants_resolv: Use it over 7(♭13), dominants resolving to minor and cinematic dominant harmony.
ar.finger_the_sixth_mode_of_melodic_minor_c: The sixth mode of melodic minor. Compared with ordinary Locrian, its natural 2nd softens the tension next to the tonic.
ar.finger_use_it_over_m75_when_a_natural_9_: Use it over m7♭5 when a natural 9 fits the harmony, especially in minor jazz ii–V–i progressions.
ar.finger_the_seventh_mode_of_melodic_minor: The seventh mode of melodic minor. Beyond 1, 3 and ♭7, it contains the altered dominant tensions ♭9, ♯9, ♭5/♯11 and ♭13.
ar.finger_use_it_over_7alt_79_79_75_or_713_: Use it over 7alt, 7♭9, 7♯9, 7♭5 or 7♭13 when a dominant chord requires strong resolution.
ar.finger_the_second_mode_of_harmonic_minor: The second mode of harmonic minor. It keeps Locrian's ♭2 and ♭5 while raising ♭6 to a natural 6th.
ar.finger_use_it_over_m75_when_a_natural_13: Use it over m7♭5 when a natural 13 fits, or for a brighter half-diminished colour than ordinary Locrian.
ar.finger_the_third_mode_of_harmonic_minor_: The third mode of harmonic minor. It is Ionian with a ♯5, creating a maj7♯5 tonic while retaining a natural 4th.
ar.finger_use_it_over_maj75_and_augmented_m: Use it over maj7♯5 and augmented-major harmony when the natural 4th is preferred to Lydian augmented's ♯4.
ar.finger_the_fourth_mode_of_harmonic_minor: The fourth mode of harmonic minor. It keeps Dorian's natural 6th while replacing the natural 4th with ♯4.
ar.finger_use_it_over_m711_fusion_metal_and: Use it over m7♯11, fusion, metal and minor vamps requiring a brighter yet tenser colour than ordinary Dorian.
ar.finger_the_fifth_mode_of_harmonic_minor_: The fifth mode of harmonic minor. Its ♭2 combined with a major 3rd creates a distinctive dominant sound unlike ordinary Phrygian.
ar.finger_use_it_over_v7_in_minor_keys_9_13: Use it over V7 in minor keys, ♭9/♭13 dominants, metal, fusion and many flamenco contexts.
ar.finger_the_sixth_mode_of_harmonic_minor_: The sixth mode of harmonic minor. It combines ♯2 with Lydian's ♯4, creating an augmented second near the tonic.
ar.finger_use_it_over_maj711_when_a_9_2_fit: Use it over maj7♯11 when a ♯9/♯2 fits the line, mainly in advanced composition and jazz contexts.
ar.finger_the_seventh_mode_of_harmonic_mino: The seventh mode of harmonic minor. It is highly tense, with ♭4, ♭5 and a doubly lowered 7th; it is not the melodic-minor Altered/Super Locrian scale.
ar.finger_use_sparingly_in_composition_dimi: Use sparingly in composition, diminished/altered harmony and advanced ear training; always read it together with its formula.
ar.finger_a_six_note_scale_built_entirely_f: A six-note scale built entirely from whole steps. With no semitones, it sounds floating and unresolved.
ar.finger_use_it_over_augmented_harmony_and: Use it over augmented harmony and dominant chords with ♯5/♭5 for an ambiguous, symmetrical colour.
ar.finger_an_eight_note_symmetrical_scale_a: An eight-note symmetrical scale alternating half and whole steps. It contains a dominant chord plus several altered tensions.
ar.finger_use_it_over_79_79_139_and_dominan: Use it over 7♭9, 7♯9, 13♭9 and dominant-diminished harmony, especially before resolution.
ar.finger_an_eight_note_symmetrical_scale_a: An eight-note symmetrical scale alternating whole and half steps. It outlines a diminished-seventh chord from the tonic.
ar.finger_use_it_over_7_harmony_diminished_: Use it over °7 harmony, diminished sequences and minor-third transposition practice.
ar.finger_the_chromatic_scale_contains_all_: The chromatic scale contains all 12 pitch classes in the octave. It is not a major-scale mode but the complete semitone collection.
ar.finger_use_it_for_technique_chromatic_ap: Use it for technique, chromatic approaches between chord tones, semitone ear training and chromatic line development.
ar.finger_mixolydian_plus_a_major_7th_passi: Mixolydian plus a major 7th passing tone. With suitable rhythmic placement, chord tones can align consistently with strong beats.
ar.finger_use_it_over_dominant_seventh_harm: Use it over dominant-seventh harmony in bebop and jazz; practise it rhythmically rather than only as a mechanical up-and-down scale.
ar.finger_a_major_scale_with_a_lowered_6th_: A major scale with a lowered 6th, combining a major tonic with the ♭6 colour often associated with minor harmony.
ar.finger_use_it_over_maj7_13_borrowed_harm: Use it over maj7(♭13), borrowed harmony and major-key lines requiring a darker colour.
ar.finger_a_major_scale_with_2_and_6_creati: A major scale with ♭2 and ♭6, creating two characteristic augmented seconds. Some Western sources also call it Byzantine.
ar.finger_use_it_for_western_labelled_middl: Use it for Western-labelled Middle Eastern/Mediterranean colours, metal, fusion and composition requiring strong tension.
ar.finger_ritusen_yo_pentatonic_mode_12456_: Ritusen/Yo pentatonic mode: 1–2–4–5–6. With G as tonic, G–A–C–D–E shares the pitches of C major pentatonic, so its open C-reference shape is valid while G stays the root (R). This differs from dominant 1–3–4–5–b7.
ar.finger_use_for_open_suspended_pentatonic: Use for open/suspended pentatonic sounds. In G, the C-major reference shape occupies open strings through fret 4; keep G as the tonal centre.
ar.finger_tuner_tools_uses_the_common_weste: Tuner Tools uses the common Western reference form 1–2–♭3–5–♭6. Naming and pitches can vary with tuning, instrument and Japanese tradition.
ar.finger_useful_for_pentatonic_melody_writ: Useful for pentatonic melody writing with wide gaps, a dark colour and interval-control practice.
ar.finger_the_western_reference_form_12457_: The Western reference form 1–♭2–4–5–♭7 creates a dark suspended colour. Traditional terminology can vary by source and tuning.
ar.finger_useful_over_sus_harmony_dark_melo: Useful over sus harmony, dark melody, ambient, metal and exercises emphasizing the ♭2.
ar.finger_the_western_reference_form_12457_: The Western reference form 1–♭2–4–♭5–♭7 has strongly tense ♭2 and ♭5 degrees. Its historical name should not be treated as one absolutely fixed Western mode.
ar.finger_useful_for_dark_melody_sound_desi: Useful for dark melody, sound design, metal and ear training with tense intervals.
ar.finger_a_custom_roman_numeral_loop_that_: A custom Roman-numeral loop that is saved automatically and transposes to every key.
ar.finger_the_dominant_of_the_target_chord_: The dominant of the target chord; its 3rd and 7th pull clearly into {0}.
ar.finger_the_diminished_chord_root_lies_a_: The diminished chord root lies a semitone below {0}, resolving upward into the destination root.
ar.finger_a_dominant_a_semitone_above_the_t: A dominant a semitone above the target, useful in jazz with a strong chromatic bass line.
ar.finger_keep_the_hand_relaxed_and_play_1_: Keep the hand relaxed and play 1-2-3-4 evenly across six strings.
ar.finger_each_finger_owns_one_fret_alterna: Each finger owns one fret; alternate picking synchronizes both hands.
ar.finger_apply_the_same_pulse_to_a_short_c: Apply the same pulse to a short chromatic line.
ar.finger_change_strings_without_breaking_t: Change strings without breaking the pulse and keep the picking motion compact.
ar.finger_alternate_picking_continues_throu: Alternate picking continues through string changes instead of restarting on each string.
ar.finger_use_this_motion_in_riffs_and_mult: Use this motion in riffs and multi-string solo lines.
ar.finger_separate_each_finger_movement_esp: Separate each finger movement, especially fingers 3 and 4.
ar.finger_lift_only_the_moving_finger_and_k: Lift only the moving finger and keep the others close to the strings.
ar.finger_prepare_for_scale_and_arpeggio_li: Prepare for scale and arpeggio lines with changing finger order.
ar.finger_keep_planted_fingers_down_while_t: Keep planted fingers down while the next finger crosses to the adjacent string.
ar.finger_the_spider_drill_develops_finger_: The Spider drill develops finger independence and two-hand string control.
ar.finger_useful_for_chords_legato_and_diag: Useful for chords, legato and diagonal string-crossing lines.
ar.finger_keep_an_even_pulse_between_1_2_3_: Keep an even pulse between 1-2-3 and 2-3-4 groups.
ar.finger_sequences_create_musical_phrasing: Sequences create musical phrasing instead of merely running straight up and down.
ar.finger_use_three_note_groups_to_build_sc: Use three-note groups to build scale-based solo phrases.
ar.finger_produce_even_notes_with_the_frett: Produce even notes with the fretting hand without repicking every note.
ar.finger_pick_the_first_note_then_articula: Pick the first note, then articulate with the fretting hand while staying in time.
ar.finger_apply_it_to_legato_phrases_and_po: Apply it to legato phrases and position connections.
